# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Formed:** 1761, from Hampshire County
- **County seat:** Pittsfield
- **Economy:** Agriculture, early textile manufacturing, iron works, and early industrialization tied to the arrival of the railroad in the late 1830s–1840s
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly English-descended New England families, with some Dutch-heritage influence from the proximity to New York
- **Religious denominations:** Congregational (dominant), Methodist, Baptist, Episcopal; smaller Quaker presence

## Boundary Changes

Berkshire County's boundaries were stable throughout the 1820–1850 period. The critical point: **vital records in Massachusetts were always recorded at the town level**, not the county level. Each town within Berkshire County maintained its own separate register. There is no county-level vital records office.

---

## Births, Marriages, and Deaths (1820–1850)

### Two Overlapping Systems

**1. Town-level recording (1639 onward):**
Massachusetts required recording of vital events at the town level from 1639. For **1820–1840**, town clerks are the *only* official recorders. Original records remain with each town's clerk.

**2. Statewide recording (1841 onward):**
Massachusetts was the first state to establish a unified statewide system, beginning in **1841**. Events from 1841–1850 should appear in *both* the town records AND the state system.

**Marriage intentions:** Commonly recorded in the bride's home town; additional recordings may be found in the groom's home town. If a marriage record is missing in one town, check the other.

**Published "Vital Records to 1850" series:** A compiled, indexed series covering more than 200 Massachusetts towns — including Berkshire County towns — and a standard first stop for the 1820–1850 period.

### Where to Look

| Source | Access |
|---|---|
| FamilySearch — "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890" (collection 2061550) | Free — [search here](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2061550) |
| Browse-only volume 004500891 (Berkshire County town clerk / town records, 1761–1850, 512 images) | Free on FamilySearch — **0% indexed, must browse image by image** |
| Massachusetts Archives, Boston (statewide records from 1841) | In-person |
| Each town clerk's office (Pittsfield, Adams, Great Barrington, Lenox, Stockbridge, North Adams, etc.) | In-person or mail request |

> ⚠️ **Gaps:** Compliance with the 1639 mandate was uneven before 1841. A negative result in the indexed collection does not mean the event was not recorded — also check the browse-only volume and the original town clerk registers.

### Church Records (Critical Substitute for 1820–1840)

When a birth, marriage, or death does not appear in town records, Congregational church registers are the first alternative.

- FamilySearch — "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (collection 1921657): [search here](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1921657)
- Browse-only volume 004500892 (Pittsfield Congregational Church Records, 1791–1850, 274 images) — **0% indexed, browse only**
- Methodist, Baptist, and Episcopal congregation records: contact denominational archives and local church offices directly

---

## Cross-Border Research (New York & Vermont)

Since the family's town borders both states, records may exist just across either line:

**New York (western border):**
- Adjacent counties: **Rensselaer County** (formed 1791) and **Columbia County** (formed 1786)
- New York had no unified statewide vital registration in this period; search town and church records in both counties
- Check FamilySearch wiki pages for those counties directly

**Vermont (northern border):**
- Adjacent county: **Bennington County** (formed 1779)
- Vermont also recorded vital events at the town level; search Bennington County towns for families near the northern Berkshire line

---

## Other Important Record Types

| Record Type | Where to Look |
|---|---|
| **Federal Census** (1820, 1830, 1840, 1850) | FamilySearch or Ancestry — note only 1850 lists all household members by name |
| **1850 Mortality Schedule** | FamilySearch / Ancestry — records deaths in the year before enumeration |
| **Probate records** | FamilySearch "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991" (collection 1678901); Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield |
| **Land / deed records** | Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, Pittsfield (county-level; complete from 1761) |
| **Military (War of 1812)** | NARA (archives.gov); Fold3 (fold3.com); Massachusetts Archives |
| **Cemetery records** | FindAGrave (findagrave.com); sexton records at individual cemeteries |
| **Newspapers** (death notices, marriages) | Newspapers.com — the *Pittsfield Sun* published notices throughout this period |
| **Naturalization** | FamilySearch "Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906" (collection 1459213) |

---

## Key Physical Repositories

| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| Berkshire County town clerk offices | Original town vital records 1820–1850 |
| Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield | Probate records |
| Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, Pittsfield | Deed books from 1761 |
| Massachusetts Archives, Boston | State vital records from 1841; statewide collections |
| New England Historic Genealogical Society (NEHGS), Boston | Largest genealogical library in the region; extensive Berkshire County materials |
| Berkshire Historical Society, Pittsfield | Local history and manuscript collections |

---

## Summary & Next Steps

Berkshire County has a solid base of surviving vital records, but the single most important thing to know is that **records are held at the individual town level** — each town kept its own birth, marriage, and death register. From 1841 the state began collecting information centrally as well.

**Recommended starting order:**
1. Identify the specific town (or towns) where your family resided
2. Search that town's entry in FamilySearch collection 2061550 ("Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890")
3. Locate the town's volume in the published *Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850* series
4. If gaps remain, browse volume 004500891 image by image and check Congregational church records
5. Because the town is near both state lines, also search adjacent Rensselaer/Columbia counties (NY) and Bennington County (VT)

Berkshire County was formed in 1761 from Hampshire County. Boundaries were stable throughout the 1820–1850 period. The important jurisdictional point is that vital records in Massachusetts were always recorded at the **town** level, not the county level — each town within Berkshire County maintained its own separate register. There is no county-level vital records office.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

Two overlapping systems apply to the 1820–1850 period:

**Town-level recording (1639 onward):** Massachusetts ordered recording of births, marriages, and deaths at the town level from 1639. [Source: Massachusetts Vital Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records]

**Statewide recording (1841 onward):** Massachusetts was the first state to establish a unified statewide recording system, beginning in 1841. **Published "Vital Records to 1850" series:** A published compilation series covering more than 200 Massachusetts towns — including Berkshire County towns — transcribes and indexes these records and is a standard first stop for the 1820–1850 period. - Original records: Each town clerk's office in Berkshire County (e.g., Pittsfield City Clerk, Adams Town Clerk, etc.)

### Church records

Congregational churches were the dominant denomination in 19th-century Berkshire County. Methodist, Baptist, and Episcopal congregations were also active.

FamilySearch holds:
- "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (collection ID 1921657), https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1921657

### Census records

- Federal census: 1820, 1830, 1840, and 1850 all cover Berkshire County. The 1820, 1830, and 1840 censuses list only heads of household by name; the 1850 census is the first to list all household members individually by name and age
- The 1850 mortality schedule records deaths in the year preceding the enumeration and is a useful source for deaths near the end of the target period

- Probate records (wills, administrations, inventories, guardianships) are particularly valuable for reconstructing family relationships when vital records are absent

Land records in Massachusetts were recorded at the county level. Per the FamilySearch wiki, Berkshire County deed books survive from the county's formation in 1761 and continue in complete runs through this period. [Source: Massachusetts Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial]

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

> **Tool-coverage note:** Every tool call for Irish-specific place and collection data returned zero results or a generic fallback. The one Ireland-specific wiki result was the **Ireland Naming Customs** page. All claims about records and repositories beyond that page are based on standard genealogical knowledge of Irish records, not confirmed tool results. Researchers should verify current holdings directly at PRONI, the National Archives of Ireland, and the FamilySearch catalog.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy
- **County:** Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland
- **Barony:** Cary (north-east County Antrim); confirm against a county map or gazetteer
- **Nearest towns:** Bushmills (immediate area); Ballycastle (nearby)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster; part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1801
- **Economy:** Mixed small-scale farming, linen production (before mechanisation concentrated it in Belfast), coastal fishing, kelp gathering, whiskey distilling (Bushmills)
- **Religious mix:** Church of Ireland (Anglican); Presbyterian (dominant Protestant dissenter in Ulster); Roman Catholic; smaller numbers of Methodists, Quakers, and Reformed Presbyterians (Covenanters)
- **Key events:** 1798 United Irishmen Rising; Act of Union 1801; Great Famine 1845–52 (mass death and emigration); expansion of Belfast linen industry; substantial emigration to North America throughout the period

---

## Boundary Changes

- Billy civil parish boundaries were stable across the target period within County Antrim.
- The **ecclesiastical parish of Billy** (Church of Ireland) is coterminous; registers labelled "Billy" refer to the same area.
- From **1864**, Billy parish fell within the **Ballycastle registration district** for civil registration. Records before 1864 are church records only.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Start date:** 1 January 1864 (all births, deaths, and non-Catholic marriages); Catholic marriages from 1 April 1845.
- **Where held:** General Register Office (GRO) of Ireland; for post-partition Ulster records, GRONI (General Register Office for Northern Ireland) in Belfast.
- **Pre-registration records:** Church registers are the **primary source** for 1780–1863 — see Church Records below.

---

### Church Records
Church registers are the **backbone** of vital-event research for this entire period.

| Denomination | Record types | Where held |
|---|---|---|
| Church of Ireland | Baptisms, marriages, burials, vestry books | PRONI (Belfast); Representative Church Body Library (Dublin) |
| Presbyterian | Baptisms, marriages, session minutes, communion rolls | PRONI; Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland (Belfast); some local congregations |
| Roman Catholic | Baptisms, marriages, burials | National Library of Ireland (digitised at **registers.nli.ie**); local parish |
| Methodist | Baptisms, marriages | PRONI; Methodist Historical Society of Ireland |

- **Language:** English; earlier Roman Catholic registers may include some Latin.
- **Finding registers:** Check the **PRONI church register database** (nidirect.gov.uk) and **registers.nli.ie** for Catholic registers before assuming a register is or is not online.
- **Coverage gap:** No specific church register volumes for Billy were returned by tools in this session; the researcher must consult PRONI and NLI directly.

---

### Census Records
- Irish census records for **1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 were almost entirely destroyed** (Four Courts fire, 1922, and earlier official destructions). Verify survival for Antrim at the National Archives of Ireland and PRONI before assuming loss.
- The **1901 and 1911 censuses** survive in full but fall outside the target period.
- **Substitutes:** See Tithe Applotment and Griffith's Valuation under Land Records; also census search lists and fragments at the National Archives of Ireland (census.nationalarchives.ie).

---

### Land Records
These records are the **most important household-level substitutes** for the destroyed census returns.

| Record | Date range | Coverage | Where held |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | c.1823–1837 | Heads of household; entire townland | National Archives of Ireland (digitised) |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | c.1847–1864 | Every occupier; north Antrim surveys c.early 1860s | National Archives of Ireland; askaboutireland.ie |
| Registry of Deeds memorials | 1708 onward | Larger landholders; deeds, wills, leases | Registry of Deeds, Dublin |
| Estate papers | Ongoing | Rentals, leases, maps for landlord estates | PRONI (check estate papers catalog) |

- **Townland is the unit:** All Irish land records are organised by **townland**, not civil parish. Identify the family's townland as early as possible.
- Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment together bracket the Famine period and serve as the primary pre-civil-registration household lists.

---

### Probate and Court Records
- **Jurisdiction:** Diocese of Connor (most of County Antrim for smaller estates); Prerogative Court of Armagh (larger estates).
- **Destruction warning:** The **1922 Four Courts fire** destroyed large volumes of pre-1900 Irish wills and administrations. Verify surviving records at the National Archives of Ireland and PRONI before assuming a record is lost.
- **Surviving substitutes:** Calendars of grants, testamentary abstracts, and some pre-1922 transcript collections.
- **Where held:** National Archives of Ireland (Dublin); PRONI (Belfast).

---

### Military Records
- **Relevant conflicts:** 1798 Rising; Napoleonic Wars (1803–1815); Crimean War (1854–1856).
- **Where held:** The National Archives, Kew (British Army service records and pension files); National Archives of Ireland (1798 rebellion and Yeomanry records); PRONI (local Yeomanry records).

---

### Cemetery Records
- **Key graveyards:** Church of Ireland graveyard at Billy (Bushmills area); Ramoan graveyard (Ballycastle area, near parish boundary).
- **Online resources:** Find A Grave (findagrave.com); Ulster Historical Foundation and local historical society transcriptions; check GRONI databases.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records held by local congregations where they survive.

---

### Newspaper Records
| Newspaper | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Belfast Newsletter | County Antrim throughout the period; one of the oldest provincial papers in the British Isles |
| Coleraine Chronicle | North Antrim area |

- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk, subscription); Linen Hall Library (Belfast); British Library.
- **Content:** Obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices, estate sales, eviction notices (Famine era), emigration ship advertisements.

---

### Immigration and Emigration Records
- **Context:** Emigration from north Antrim to North America was heavy throughout 1780–1870, most intense during and after the Famine (1845–1855). Major embarkation ports: Londonderry (Derry), Belfast, Liverpool, Glasgow.
- **Record types:** US passenger arrival manifests (name-indexed at Ancestry and FamilySearch for post-1820 arrivals); Canadian arrival series; naturalization records in the destination country; estate-assisted emigration papers.
- **Where held:** NARA (US arrivals); Library and Archives Canada; National Archives of Ireland (some assisted-emigration records); PRONI (estate-assisted emigration records).

---

### Other Record Types

| Record type | Date range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Ordnance Survey Memoirs | 1830s | Detailed parish descriptions for Ulster; Billy almost certainly covered. Published by Institute of Irish Studies, QUB; held at Royal Irish Academy and PRONI |
| Church of Ireland vestry books | Ongoing | Local administration, poor relief, cess levies; Representative Church Body Library and PRONI |
| Poor Law records | From 1838 | Ballymoney and/or Ballycastle Poor Law Union; Board of Guardians minute books, relief registers, workhouse records at PRONI |
| Grand Jury presentments | Ongoing | County-level tax for roads and bridges; National Archives of Ireland |
| Ordnance Survey Name Books | 1830s | Townland spellings and local usage; National Archives of Ireland |

---

## Repository Guide

### Online Repositories

| Repository | Relevance | Access |
|---|---|---|
| registers.nli.ie | Digitised Roman Catholic parish registers for all Ireland | Free |
| PRONI Online (nidirect.gov.uk) | Antrim church registers, estate papers, street directories | Free |
| National Archives of Ireland (census.nationalarchives.ie) | Surviving census fragments, Tithe Applotment, surviving wills | Free |
| askaboutireland.ie | Griffith's Valuation digitised | Free |
| British Newspaper Archive | Ulster newspapers | Subscription |
| Ancestry.com | Some Irish passenger lists, civil registration indexes | Subscription |
| FindMyPast (findmypast.com) | Irish records including BMD indexes, Ulster newspapers | Subscription |

**FamilySearch Catalog:** Check https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog by entering "Antrim" as the place; tools could not resolve Irish place identifiers in this session, so no FamilySearch collection or volume data could be confirmed.

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| **PRONI, Belfast** | Church registers, estate papers, Poor Law records, tithe maps, Ordnance Survey |
| **Representative Church Body Library, Dublin** | Church of Ireland vestry and register originals |
| **National Archives of Ireland, Dublin** | Census fragments, wills/administrations, tithe applotment, transportation records |
| **Presbyterian Historical Society, Belfast** | Presbyterian registers and minutes for Ulster |
| **Registry of Deeds, Dublin** | Deed memorials from 1708 |
| **The National Archives, Kew (UK)** | British Army service records, pension files |
| **Royal Irish Academy, Dublin** | Ordnance Survey Memoir drafts and field notebooks |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 Four Courts fire (Dublin):** Destroyed large volumes of pre-1900 Irish wills, administration bonds, and pre-Famine census returns. Verify what specifically survives for Antrim at the National Archives of Ireland before assuming a record is gone.
- **Pre-Famine census returns:** Census records for 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 are largely destroyed; use Tithe Applotment and Griffith's Valuation as substitutes.
- **Church register gaps:** Not all registers begin at the same date; some were not kept consistently during periods of clergy vacancy or disruption.

---

## Naming Conventions

*(Based on the FamilySearch Wiki, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs)*

- **Traditional naming pattern** (a clue, not a rigid rule): First son → father's father; second son → mother's father; third son → father; fourth son → father's eldest brother; first daughter → mother's mother; second daughter → father's mother; third daughter → mother. A broken pattern is not evidence of non-identity.
- **Mac and O prefixes** were frequently dropped and restored across time and record types: the same family may appear as O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn within a single parish.
- **Spelling was not standardised**; a single family's surname may appear in multiple spellings across records.
- **Given name anglicisation:** Many Gaelic given names were anglicised, producing wide variation. Darby, Dermot, and Jeremiah, for example, can all represent the same underlying name. Some given names were used for both sexes (Florence, Sydney, Evelyn).

---

## Adjoining Parishes

Families near the edges of Billy civil parish may appear in registers and records of neighbouring parishes. Check:
- **Ramoan** (east, Ballycastle area)
- **Culfeightrin** (east/north)
- **Ballintoy** (west)

---

## Research Sequence

1. **Identify the townland** — use Griffith's Valuation (askaboutireland.ie) or the Townland Index. The townland, not the civil parish, is the key to all Irish records.
2. **Identify the family's religion** — Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, or Roman Catholic registers are entirely separate.
3. **Check PRONI's church register database** and **registers.nli.ie** to find which registers survive and where they are held.
4. **Search Tithe Applotment Books** (c.1823–1837) to locate the family before the Famine.
5. **Search church registers** for baptisms, marriages, and burials.
6. **Check probate calendars** at the National Archives of Ireland for any testamentary records, noting the 1922 destruction.
7. **Search estate papers at PRONI** for landlord-tenant records covering the family's townland.
8. **Search emigration records** if the family left Ireland, beginning with passenger arrival manifests and then naturalization records in the destination jurisdiction.
9. **Check the Ordnance Survey Memoirs** for narrative and contextual detail about the parish in the 1830s.

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy
- **County:** Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland
- **Barony:** The civil parish of Billy falls within the barony of Cary in the north-east of County Antrim. The FamilySearch Wiki did not return a county-level or parish-level page in this session; the barony and neighboring parishes should be confirmed against a county map or gazetteer before routing searches.
- **County seat / administrative center:** Antrim town (county administration); the nearest market town to Billy parish is Bushmills, with Ballycastle also nearby.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim sits within the historic province of Ulster, which became part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland in 1801 (Act of Union).
- **Population during period:** No population figures were returned by tools for this parish or county. The researcher should consult the General Report of the Census of Ireland for 1841 and 1851, which include parish-level population tables.
- **Economy:** The north Antrim coast economy during this period combined small-scale mixed farming, linen production (especially in earlier decades, before mechanization concentrated the trade in Belfast), coastal fishing, and some kelp gathering. The Bushmills area is associated with whiskey distilling.
- **Ethnic composition:** The plantation of Ulster in the early seventeenth century brought Scottish and English settlers alongside the existing Gaelic Irish population. By 1780–1870, north Antrim had a substantial Presbyterian community of Scottish descent, a Church of Ireland (Anglican) population largely descended from English settlers and Gaelic converts, and a smaller Roman Catholic community. The mix is directly relevant to which church registers survive for which families.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of Ireland (established church); Presbyterian (the dominant Protestant dissenting body in Ulster); Roman Catholic; also smaller numbers of Methodists, Quakers, and Reformed Presbyterians (Covenanters). Billy civil parish was served by the Church of Ireland parish church of Billy (at Bushmills). Presbyterian congregations in the area include Bushmills (Route Presbytery), and the Roman Catholic parish covering the area was Ramoan/Ballycastle and/or the Bushmills district — the researcher must confirm actual congregational coverage against the PRONI church register index before selecting registers to search.
- **Key historical events:** The 1798 United Irishmen Rising affected Ulster; the Act of Union 1801; the Great Famine 1845–52 (severe depopulation throughout Ireland, including Antrim, through death and emigration); the expansion of the linen industry centred on Belfast; and substantial emigration to North America throughout the period.

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish boundaries were stable within County Antrim across the target period. No boundary split was returned by tools.
- The ecclesiastical parish of Billy (Church of Ireland) is a distinct but coterminous unit; records labeled "Billy" in church registers refer to the same geographic area.
- The registration district system introduced for civil registration in 1864 placed Billy parish within the Ballycastle registration district. Records created before 1864 fall under church registration only. The researcher should confirm the registration district assignment against the PRONI or GRO (Ireland) district maps, as tools did not return this assignment.

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland vital records (including `Ireland_Vital_Records`) all returned generic fallback content in this session; no Ireland-specific start date was returned. The researcher should consult the FamilySearch Wiki page at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Vital_Records directly. The researcher should also consult the General Register Office (GRO) of Ireland.
- **What exists:** Tools returned no collection records for civil registration in County Antrim. The tools did not confirm what specific registers survive.
- **Where held:** The researcher should consult the General Register Office, Government of Ireland (for births, marriages, and deaths from 1864), and the PRONI (Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Belfast) for later Ulster records.
- **Gaps:** Because nearly the entire target period (1780–1863) predates civil registration, church registers are the primary source for vital events. See Church Records below.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers of baptism, marriage, and burial — see below.

### Church records

- **Denominations present:** Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Roman Catholic, Methodist. The mix is critical: a family's religion determines which register to search.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (not births), marriages, burials. Confirmation records exist for some Church of Ireland and Roman Catholic registers and are a separate dated event that can fall years after baptism.
- **Where held:** The researcher should search the PRONI church register index (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/services/search-historical-records-online) and the Representative Church Body Library (Dublin) for Church of Ireland registers. Presbyterian registers for the Route Presbytery area are held partly at PRONI and partly by local congregations or the Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland (Belfast). Roman Catholic registers are at local parish level or on microfilm/digital at the National Library of Ireland (https://registers.nli.ie/).
- **Language:** English. Earlier Roman Catholic registers may contain some Latin, particularly in the sacramental formula.
- **Coverage gap:** No specific church register volumes for Billy parish were returned by `volume_search` or `collections_search` in this session; both tools returned zero results. The researcher must check the PRONI church record database and the National Library of Ireland's digitised Catholic registers directly.

### Census records

- **Federal/national census:** The FamilySearch Wiki page for Ireland Census (attempted at `https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Census`) returned only a generic fallback page in this session. No census collection records for Ireland were returned by `collections_search` or `volume_search`.
- **Known gap of major importance:** Irish census records for 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 were almost entirely destroyed — but the tools did not state this for County Antrim specifically, so the researcher should confirm the situation for Antrim at the National Archives of Ireland and PRONI before assuming loss. The 1901 and 1911 censuses are outside the target period.
- **Surviving substitutes:** Census search lists and census fragments at the National Archives of Ireland (Dublin) and PRONI should be checked. The researcher should consult https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/ for what survives.
- **State/provincial census:** No tool result returned an Irish provincial or county census for this period.

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories.
- **Holding level:** Probate in Ireland for this period was handled by the Prerogative Court of Armagh (for estates valued above a certain threshold) and the Diocesan Consistorial Court of Connor (which had jurisdiction over County Antrim for smaller estates). The diocese of Connor (later Connor and Down) covered most of County Antrim.
- **Known destruction:** A significant proportion of pre-1900 Irish wills and administrations were destroyed in the 1922 Four Courts fire (Dublin). Tools did not state this for Antrim specifically; the researcher must verify surviving records through the National Archives of Ireland and PRONI. Surviving testamentary abstracts and calendar of grants exist and should be checked.
- **Where held:** National Archives of Ireland (Dublin) for surviving originals; PRONI for Ulster records; FamilySearch has microfilmed some Irish probate calendars — but `volume_search` returned no results for Ireland in this session, so the extent of microfilm coverage is unconfirmed.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Ireland used a townland-based system. The townland is the smallest unit and is the key to locating records. Billy civil parish contains multiple townlands; the researcher should identify the specific townland of interest using the Townland Index or the Ordnance Survey Name Books.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The FamilySearch Wiki page for `Ireland_Land_and_Property` returned only a generic fallback page in this session. The researcher should consult that page directly.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (c.1823–1837):** List heads of household who paid the tithe; cover most of Ireland including County Antrim. These are one of the most important pre-Famine household lists and partially substitute for lost census records. Tools did not return collection details for these in this session.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** A property valuation listing every occupier; for north Antrim, surveys were conducted in the early 1860s. One of the most important mid-nineteenth-century resources for locating families by townland. Available online; tools did not return a specific URL in this session.
- **Registry of Deeds (Dublin):** Memorials of deeds, wills, and leases from 1708 onward; relevant for larger landholders.
- **Estate papers:** Many north Antrim townlands were held by large landlord estates; estate records (rentals, leases, maps) can be rich substitutes. Check PRONI's estate papers catalog.
- **Where held:** National Archives of Ireland (Dublin); PRONI (Belfast); Registry of Deeds (Dublin).

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** 1798 Rising; Napoleonic Wars (1803–1815); Crimean War (1854–1856); no major conflict on Irish soil in the later part of the period.
- **Record types:** Service records and pension files for men who served in the British Army are held at The National Archives (Kew, UK). Muster rolls and description books are at Kew. The 1798 rebellion generated rebel prisoner lists and some Yeomanry records at the National Archives of Ireland and PRONI.
- **Where held:** The National Archives, Kew (British Army records); National Archives of Ireland (1798 rebellion records); PRONI (local Yeomanry records).
- **Coverage gap:** No military collection volumes were returned by `volume_search` for Ireland in this session.

### Cemetery records

- **Major cemeteries:** Billy parish contains Church of Ireland and Roman Catholic burial grounds. The Church of Ireland graveyard at Billy (Bushmills area) is one primary site. The researcher should also check Ramoan graveyard (Ballycastle area) for families near the parish boundary.
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) is a general resource; the tool returned it as a generic link not filtered to Ireland. The Ulster Historical Foundation and local historical societies have transcribed some Antrim graveyards. GRONI (Graves Records of Northern Ireland) databases should be checked.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records, where they survive, are typically held by the local congregation.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The Coleraine Chronicle and the Belfast Newsletter are the primary newspapers covering north Antrim in this period. The Belfast Newsletter is one of the oldest provincial newspapers in the British Isles and carried notices for County Antrim throughout the target period.
- **Where held:** The British Newspaper Archive (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) holds digitised copies of several Ulster newspapers. The Linen Hall Library (Belfast) and the British Library hold physical collections. Tools did not return a specific collection record for these.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices (including estate sales and eviction notices during the Famine), and emigration ship advertisements.

### Immigration and emigration records

- **Context:** Emigration from north Antrim to North America was substantial throughout 1780–1870 and especially intense during and after the Famine (1845–1855). Many emigrants sailed from the ports of Derry/Londonderry, Belfast, Liverpool, and Glasgow.
- **Relevant ports:** Londonderry (Derry) was a major embarkation port for Ulster emigrants to North America. Passenger manifests for US-bound arrivals are at NARA (for post-1820 arrivals). Pre-1820 passenger lists are fragmentary.
- **Record types:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests, name-indexed on Ancestry and FamilySearch for many US arrivals); Canadian arrivals have their own series. Naturalization records in the destination country. Assisted-emigration records where an estate or the British government funded the passage.
- **Content note:** Arrival manifests list all passengers including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest page for all family members.
- **Where held:** NARA (US arrivals); Library and Archives Canada; National Archives of Ireland (some assisted-emigration records); PRONI (estate-assisted emigration records).
- **Coverage gap:** No emigration or passenger list volumes for Ireland were returned by `volume_search` in this session.

### Tax records

- **Types:** Hearth Money Rolls (pre-target period but useful for earlier generations); Tithe Applotment Books (c.1823–1837, see Land Records above); Grand Jury presentments (county-level taxation for road and bridge maintenance).
- **Date range:** Tithe Applotment (c.1823–1837) falls within the target period and is among the most important early-nineteenth-century household lists.
- **Where held:** National Archives of Ireland; also widely digitised — the researcher should check the National Archives of Ireland website directly.
- **Substitute value:** The Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation together bracket the Famine period and partially substitute for the destroyed census records.

### Other record types

- **Ordnance Survey Memoirs (1830s):** The Ordnance Survey of Ireland compiled detailed parish memoirs for Ulster in the 1830s, describing the economy, natural features, population, and traditions of each parish. Billy parish is almost certainly covered. The memoirs are published (Institute of Irish Studies, Queen's University Belfast, 1990s series) and held at the Royal Irish Academy and PRONI.
- **Church vestry records:** Church of Ireland vestry books record local church administration, poor relief, road maintenance, and cess (local tax) levies, and can name householders not in other records. Check the Representative Church Body Library and PRONI.
- **Poor Law records:** The Ballymoney Poor Law Union (and possibly the Ballycastle Union) covered north Antrim from 1838. Board of Guardian minute books, relief registers, and workhouse records survive at PRONI and partially at the National Archives of Ireland.
- **Local and county histories:** The Ordnance Survey Memoirs, Bassett's County Antrim Guide and Directory (1888), and various Ulster Journal of Archaeology articles provide context and sometimes name individuals.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| Repository | Relevance to this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| National Library of Ireland (registers.nli.ie) | Digitised Roman Catholic parish registers for Ireland | Free |
| PRONI Online (nidirect.gov.uk) | Antrim church registers, estate papers, street directories | Free |
| British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk) | Ulster newspapers including Belfast Newsletter, Coleraine Chronicle | Subscription |
| National Archives of Ireland (census.nationalarchives.ie) | Surviving census fragments; Tithe Applotment; wills | Free |
| Ancestry.com | Some Irish passenger lists, civil registration indexes | Subscription |
| FindMyPast (findmypast.com) | Irish records including BMD indexes, newspapers | Subscription |

Note: The tools returned no collection records, volume records, or curated external links specific to Ireland or County Antrim in this session. The repositories listed above were not returned by any tool result; the researcher should verify current holdings directly. The `external_links_search` tool returned only six generic US-focused links (FindAGrave, Fold3, Ancestry US Census, Newspapers.com, NARA, and FamilySearch Vital Records wiki) that are not specific to Ireland.

**Coverage of this survey:** `volume_search` returned 0 results for Ireland; `collections_search` returned 0 results. No digitized volume or indexed collection data was available from the tools in this session. The FamilySearch catalog could not be queried because `place_search` returned no standard place for any Irish location, which is required by `collections_search` and `volume_search`. The researcher must check FamilySearch's catalog directly at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog by entering "Antrim" as the place.

### Physical repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| PRONI, Belfast | Church registers, estate papers, Poor Law records, tithe maps, Ordnance Survey | In-person; many records digitised at PRONI online |
| Representative Church Body Library, Dublin | Church of Ireland vestry and register originals | In-person; some records on microfilm/digital |
| National Archives of Ireland, Dublin | Census fragments, wills/administrations, tithe applotment, transportation records | In-person; major record sets online |
| Presbyterian Historical Society, Belfast | Presbyterian registers and minutes for Ulster | In-person; contact for access |
| Registry of Deeds, Dublin | Deed memorials from 1708 | In-person; indexes available |
| The National Archives, Kew (UK) | British Army service records, pension files | In-person; many records on Ancestry/Findmypast |

## Records NOT online

The following record types are not confirmed as online by any tool result in this session and likely require physical access or correspondence:

- Church of Ireland vestry books for Billy parish
- Grand Jury presentments for County Antrim
- Estate rentals and leases for north Antrim landlord estates
- Presbyterian session minutes and communion rolls
- Poor Law Board of Guardians minute books (Ballymoney / Ballycastle unions)
- Ordnance Survey field notebooks and memoir drafts (unpublished material at RIA and PRONI)

## Known record losses

No tool result in this session stated a specific record loss for Billy civil parish or County Antrim. The researcher should verify the following known Irish record destruction events against the specific record sets of interest, as tools did not confirm the scope for Antrim:

- The destruction of the Public Record Office of Ireland in the Four Courts fire (Dublin, 1922) destroyed large volumes of pre-1900 Irish wills, administration bonds, and pre-Famine census returns. Whether specific Antrim materials were among those destroyed must be confirmed at the National Archives of Ireland.
- The researcher should consult PRONI's records destruction schedules and finding aids for what was duplicated or survived in Ulster before assuming a record is lost.

## Research tips

- **Naming customs (from the FamilySearch Wiki, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs):** A traditional naming pattern was often used by Irish parents until the later nineteenth century: the first son was usually named for the father's father; the second son for the mother's father; the third son for the father; the fourth son for the father's eldest brother; the first daughter for the mother's mother; the second daughter for the father's mother; and the third daughter for the mother. The pattern is a clue, not a rule — it was not universally followed, and a broken pattern is not evidence of non-identity.
- **Surname variation (from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs):** Mac and O prefixes in Irish surnames were frequently dropped or restored over time, so the same family may appear as O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn across records. Spelling was not standardised; a single family's surname may be recorded several ways in one parish.
- **Given name anglicisation (from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs):** Many Gaelic given names were anglicised, producing variation. Darby, Dermot, and Jeremiah, for example, are all variations of the same underlying name. Some given names were used for both males and females (Florence, Sydney, Evelyn).
- **Religion determines which register to search:** In Ulster, knowing whether a family was Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, or Roman Catholic is essential before selecting a register. The three denominations maintained entirely separate records. A family misidentified as Church of Ireland when it was Presbyterian will not appear in the Church of Ireland register.
- **Townland is the unit, not the civil parish:** All Irish land records, church registers, and valuations are organised by townland. Identify the townland of the family of interest as early as possible; searching at civil-parish level will locate the townland entry, but the researcher must then track the townland across registers, valuations, and maps as a unit.
- **Tithe Applotment + Griffith's as a census substitute:** Because Irish census returns for 1821–1851 are largely destroyed, the Tithe Applotment Books (c.1823–1837) and Griffith's Primary Valuation (c.1847–1864) together bracket the Famine period and serve as the primary household-level records for that era. They list heads of household only, not full family members.
- **Adjoining parishes:** Families in Billy civil parish lived near the borders of Ramoan, Culfeightrin, and Ballintoy parishes in County Antrim, and families near the coast crossed denominational and civil-parish lines regularly. The researcher should search the registers and land records of these neighboring parishes as well. The FamilySearch Wiki county page for Antrim was not returned by tools in this session; the researcher should check the neighboring-parishes table there directly.
- **Emigration destination research:** For families who emigrated during or after the Famine, North American passenger arrivals (especially at New York, Baltimore, Philadelphia, Quebec, and Saint John) should be searched. Naturalization records in the destination jurisdiction will often record the county or parish of origin in Ireland, especially post-1906 US petitions.
- **Research sequence:** Start with Griffith's Valuation to locate the family by townland; work backward using Tithe Applotment; search church registers (identify denomination first); check PRONI's church register index for what survives and where; search probate calendars at the National Archives of Ireland for any testamentary records; check estate papers at PRONI for landlord-tenant records.

---

Billy civil parish sits in the north-east corner of County Antrim, an area shaped by the Ulster plantation, strong Presbyterian and Church of Ireland communities, and heavy emigration during and after the Great Famine. For the period 1780 to 1870 almost all records of births, marriages, and deaths are found in church registers rather than civil records, because Irish national civil registration did not begin until 1864. Those registers, along with the Tithe Applotment Books of the 1820s–1830s and Griffith's Valuation of the 1860s, are the backbone of research for this time and place, and most are held at PRONI in Belfast or the National Library of Ireland online. The most important warning is that the tools available in this session were unable to resolve any Irish place or return any Ireland-specific collection data, so collection counts, volume details, and digitisation levels could not be confirmed; the researcher should check the FamilySearch catalog at familysearch.org/search/catalog and the PRONI church register database directly before assuming any specific register is or is not online.

The next step is to consult the FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland and County Antrim directly (the tool infrastructure returned only generic fallback content for those URLs in this session), and to identify the specific townland and religious denomination of the family of interest before routing searches to the appropriate registers at PRONI or the National Library of Ireland.

Locality guide **loc_001** has been saved to the project. Here is a summary of what it covers:

---

## Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania — Locality Research Guide (1840–1880)

**County background:** Formed in 1811; heavily industrialized with coal mining by mid-19th century, drawing large immigrant populations (Irish, Welsh, German).

### Records Available on FamilySearch (5 digitized volumes)

| Collection | Date Range | Indexing |
|---|---|---|
| Deed Records | 1815–1900 | Partially indexed (~22%) |
| Probate Records | 1851–1930 | Image browse only |
| Naturalization Records | 1849–1915 | Image browse only |
| Church Records | 1842–1895 | Image browse only; partly German-language |

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (Bushmills area), Ireland — 1780–1870

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, in the barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Principal town:** Bushmills; also includes Dervock, Stranocum, and surrounding townlands
- **Key note on partition:** After 1922, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland (United Kingdom). Records are held at **PRONI** (Belfast) and sometimes duplicated at the National Archives of Ireland (Dublin).
- **Religious composition:** The Bushmills area was historically Protestant-majority (Church of Ireland and Presbyterian), but a significant Catholic population was present. In 1861, Protestants made up roughly 60% and Catholics roughly 40% of County Antrim.

---

## Civil Registration

- **Start date:** Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths began across all of Ireland **on 1 January 1864**.
- **Coverage in your window:** Only the last six years (1864–1870) fall within civil registration. The period 1780–1863 is **not covered** — church registers are the only systematic vital record source for those 84 years.
- **Where held:** **GRONI** (General Register Office Northern Ireland), Belfast, holds civil registration records for County Antrim.

---

## Church Records (Primary Source for 1780–1863)

### Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)

> **Are Church of Ireland registers available?** — Yes, but with significant caveats.

The **1922 fire** at the Public Record Office in Dublin destroyed roughly **two-thirds** of all Church of Ireland parish registers that had been deposited there. However:

- Many County Antrim registers were **never deposited** in Dublin, or copies had already been made
- **PRONI** holds surviving Church of Ireland registers for Northern Ireland, either as originals or microfilm copies
- The **RCB Library** (Dublin) also holds some surviving registers
- Whether the Billy/Bushmills Church of Ireland registers survived the 1922 fire is **not confirmed** — you must check:
  - [PRONI's Guide to Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf)
  - [RCB Library Parish Register List](https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf)
  - [PRONI Digitised Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1)

**Online access:**
| Collection | Platform | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Irish Parish Register Baptisms/Confirmations, Ffolliott Collection | FindMyPast | $ |
| Irish Parish Register Marriages, Ffolliott Collection | FindMyPast | $ |
| Irish Parish Register Burials, Ffolliott Collection | FindMyPast | $ |
| Ireland, Diocesan & Prerogative Marriage License Bonds, 1623–1866 | FamilySearch (collection/3460239) | Free |

### Roman Catholic

- Catholic registers in rural County Antrim generally **did not begin until Catholic Emancipation in 1828**, though some may start from the mid-1700s
- The relevant diocese is **Down and Connor**
- **Note:** Catholic parish boundaries differ from civil parish boundaries; identify the relevant Catholic parish separately

**Online access:**
| Collection | Platform | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 | National Library of Ireland: [registers.nli.ie](https://registers.nli.ie/) | Free |
| Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 | Ancestry | $ |
| Ireland Roman Catholic Parish Marriages | FindMyPast | $ |

### Presbyterian

- Many Presbyterian registers in Ulster date from the 1600s; the average start date nationally is around 1830, but the Bushmills area was heavily settled by Scottish Presbyterians from 1605, so registers may begin earlier
- **PRONI** holds many Presbyterian registers for County Antrim

**Online access:**
| Collection | Platform | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Ireland, Non-Conformist Births and Baptisms | FindMyPast | $ |
| Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages | FindMyPast | $ |
| Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials | FindMyPast | $ |
| Ulster Historical Foundation | [ancestryireland.com](https://www.ancestryireland.com) | Varies |

---

## Census Records & Substitutes

Full Irish census records for this period largely do not survive. The main substitutes are:

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837)** — lists of landholders liable for tithe payments; covers most townlands in County Antrim
- **Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864)** — comprehensive land survey listing heads of household; essential for locating families in the pre-census era
- These are available on **AskAboutIreland.ie** (free) and **IrishOrigins.com** ($)

---

## Probate & Estate Records

The 1922 Dublin fire destroyed most original pre-partition will files, but indexes and abstracts survive. Key substitute collections:

| Collection | Platform | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Betham Genealogical Abstracts | FindMyPast | Free |
| Thrift Genealogical Abstracts | FindMyPast | Free |
| Crossle Genealogical Abstracts | FindMyPast | Free |
| Indexes to Wills, Probate, Marriage Bonds & Licences, 1591–1866 | Ancestry | $ |
| Ireland, Abstracts of Wills and Marriages, 1620–1923 | Ancestry | $ |

**PRONI** also holds estate papers for landlord estates in the Bushmills/County Antrim area — these can name individual tenants with considerable detail.

---

## Repository Summary

| Repository | What's held | Contact/Access |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI**, 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church registers (CoI, Presbyterian); land records; census substitutes; estate papers; much more | [nidirect.gov.uk/proni](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni) / proni@communities-ni.gov.uk / 028 9053 4800 |
| **GRONI**, Belfast | Civil registration (births/marriages/deaths from 1864) | [nidirect.gov.uk/gro](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/searching-historical-records) |
| **RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Dublin 14 | Surviving Church of Ireland registers | [ireland.anglican.org](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) / library@ireland.anglican.org |
| **National Archives of Ireland**, Dublin | Pre-1922 national records; some census fragments | [nationalarchives.ie](https://www.nationalarchives.ie/) |
| **National Library of Ireland** | Catholic parish registers online | [registers.nli.ie](https://registers.nli.ie/) — Free |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 Dublin PRO fire:** Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers deposited there were destroyed. County Antrim registers that were not deposited (or had been copied) may survive at PRONI or the RCB Library.
- **Irish census records:** Most 19th-century census returns for Ireland did not survive; use Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation as substitutes.

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Search all three denominations** (Church of Ireland, Catholic, Presbyterian) — families in mixed communities sometimes appear in registers outside their own faith.
2. **Catholic parish boundaries differ from civil parish boundaries.** Identify the correct Catholic parish for the Bushmills area separately from the civil parish of Billy.
3. Check **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** first to confirm which registers survive for Billy/Bushmills and their start dates before assuming a record is lost.
4. **Civil registration begins only in 1864** — for any event before that date, church registers are your primary source.
5. Use the **Betham, Thrift, and Crossle abstracts** on FindMyPast as substitutes for probate records lost in 1922.
6. PRONI offers a free enquiry service and a fee-paying copy/search service: [PRONI Enquiry Service](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/proni-enquiry-service).

## Known record losses

The FamilySearch Wiki page on Ireland Church Records (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states: "Church of Ireland (Anglican, Episcopalian) [records] began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922." This refers to the fire at the Public Record Office in Dublin in June 1922. Registers that had been deposited at the Dublin PRO were lost. However:

- Many Northern Ireland (County Antrim) Church of Ireland registers were never deposited at the Dublin PRO, or copies had already been made; PRONI holds a substantial set of surviving registers
- Whether the Billy/Bushmills parish registers were among those lost or those that survived is not confirmed by the tools. Consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records and the RCB Library register list (both URLs given above) to determine what specifically survives for this parish

The Betham, Thrift, and Crossle genealogical abstracts (all on FindMyPast) are described by the Ireland Church Records page as "useful substitute[s] to records lost in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin."

Census returns for Ireland: the Ireland Census wiki page returned only a generic fallback page in this session, so the fate of specific Irish census returns for 1780–1870 cannot be confirmed from tool results. Consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Census directly.

## Research tips

All tips below are drawn from the FamilySearch Wiki Ireland Church Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) unless otherwise noted.

- "Search all parish registers and other available church records of the appropriate locality for the time period you are researching." For the Billy civil parish area, this means searching Church of Ireland, Catholic, and Presbyterian registers, not just the denomination you believe your family belonged to.
- "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland." Mixed-denomination communities in County Antrim meant that Catholic or Presbyterian families sometimes appear in Church of Ireland registers.
- "Catholics had different parish boundaries to the Church of Ireland." Civil parishes (like Billy) match Church of Ireland parish boundaries but do not match Catholic parish boundaries. For Catholic records, identify the relevant Catholic parish separately; it may be named differently and serve a different geographic area.
- "Search surrounding localities if you cannot find records in the expected locality." Neighbouring parishes for the Bushmills/Billy area include Armoy, Ballintoy, Dunluce, and Ballymoney. The wiki page for County Antrim's neighbouring counties/parishes did not return from tools, so a complete adjacency list is not confirmed by tool results.
- "Note gaps or missing pages in the record. You may want to search alternative records for the missing time periods." This is particularly important given the 1922 losses.
- Identifying the religion of research subjects "will greatly increase the chance of success." The Bushmills area was historically Protestant-majority with Church of Ireland and Presbyterian families predominating, but a significant Catholic population was also present.
- In Northern Ireland, County Antrim is one of the six counties that remained in the United Kingdom after 1922. Records therefore fall under PRONI (not the National Archives of Ireland) for post-1922 administration, but copies of many pre-1922 national records are available at both repositories.
- The Betham Genealogical Abstracts on FindMyPast are a key substitute source for any records lost in the 1922 fire.
- PRONI provides a free enquiry service and a fee-paying copy and search service: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/proni-enquiry-service

Billy civil parish (the Bushmills area) sits in northern County Antrim, now in Northern Ireland. The most important thing to know about this period (1780–1870) is that civil birth, marriage, and death registration did not begin until 1864, so church registers are the only systematic vital record source for most of those ninety years. Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic registers all exist for this area, though a major fire in Dublin in 1922 destroyed roughly two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers that had been deposited there; surviving registers for County Antrim are mostly held at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) in Belfast, and some are now digitised and searchable online through PRONI's website and FindMyPast. # Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy | **Barony:** Carey / Lower Dunluce | **Poor law union:** Coleraine
- **County:** Antrim, Ulster Province → from 1921, Northern Ireland (UK)
- **Centre:** Bushmills (north Antrim coast)
- **Predominant religious makeup:** Scots-Ulster Protestant (Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Covenanters, Wesleyan Methodist) alongside a Catholic Irish minority — legacy of the Ulster Plantation
- **Key historical events:** 1798 Rebellion; Napoleonic Wars; Irish Famine (1845–52); 1922 PRO Dublin fire (destroys many Church of Ireland registers)

---

## Boundary & Ecclesiastical Notes

- Billy was the **head of an ecclesiastical union** also comprising **Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride** — search all five parishes when Billy registers are missing.
- Civil boundaries were stable throughout the period.
- **Critical custody shift:** After 1921, County Antrim record custody moved to PRONI (Belfast) and GRONI; some pre-1921 originals remained in Dublin (destroyed 1922).

---

## The Core Research Challenge

**Civil registration did not begin until 1 January 1864** (non-Catholic marriages from 1845). For the years **1780–1863**, church registers are the *only* primary source for births, marriages, and deaths.

The FamilySearch wiki page for Billy Civil Parish lists denomination headings but provides **no specific register dates or PRONI reference numbers**. The PRONI *Guide to Church Records* PDF is the indispensable first step.

---

## Church Records — Closing the Gap

### Step 1: Identify surviving registers

**PRONI — Public Record Office of Northern Ireland**
2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ
📧 proni@communities-ni.gov.uk | ☎ 028 9053 4800

- **Guide to Church Records (PDF):** https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf — lists every surviving register, its date range, and PRONI microfilm reference. **Download this first.**
- **Digitised registers viewable online:** https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- **eCATALOGUE (search by parish):** https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/services/proni-online-public-access
- Church of Ireland registers: MIC1 series; Presbyterian: MIC1P series

**RCB Library — Church of Ireland**
Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735
📧 library@ireland.anglican.org | ☎ +353 (0)1 492 3979
- Register survival list: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
- Many registers not destroyed in 1922 are here.

### Step 2: Online indexes by denomination

| Denomination | Database | URL | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Catholic** | NLI Catholic Parish Registers | https://registers.nli.ie/ | Free |
| **Catholic** | Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915 | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/ | Subscription |
| **All — marriage bonds** | Ireland, Diocesan & Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866 | https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 | Free |
| **Presbyterian & Non-Conformist** | Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms | Subscription |
| **Presbyterian & Non-Conformist** | Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages | Subscription |
| **Presbyterian & Non-Conformist** | Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-burials | Subscription |
| **Church of Ireland (Ffolliott)** | Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection | Subscription |
| **All (Ulster focus)** | RootsIreland / Ulster Historical Foundation | http://www.rootsireland.ie/ | Subscription |
| **All (Ulster focus)** | AncestryIreland | http://www.ancestryireland.com/ | Subscription |
| **All (broad)** | Irish Records Index, 1500–1920 | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/4077 | Subscription |
| **Post-1922 fire substitute** | Betham Genealogical Abstracts | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts | Subscription |

> **Catholic coverage note:** Rural Ulster Catholic registers typically begin 1820s–1840s; expect a gap for 1780–c.1820.
> **Presbyterian coverage note:** Most start c. 1830; for 1780–1830, use Betham/Thrift abstracts and estate papers.
> **Covenanters:** Use PRONI Guide first; FindMyPast Non-Conformist collections may include some.

---

## Census & Census Substitutes

| Record | Coverage | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837)** | Landholders in every townland | FamilySearch https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1804886; National Archives Ireland |
| **Griffith's Primary Valuation (c. 1861)** | All property occupiers by townland | Free: https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/; also Ancestry, FindMyPast |
| **Flax Growers' List (1796)** | Linen weavers who received spinning wheels | Various archives |
| **1901/1911 Censuses** | Full census (post-period; very useful for persistence) | Free: https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/ |

> **Note:** The 1861, 1871, 1881, and 1891 Irish censuses were destroyed by government order. The 1821–1851 survive only in fragments (pension applications). For 1780–1823, Hearth Tax lists and estate papers are the only household-level substitutes.

---

## Civil Registration (1864–1870)

**GRONI — General Register Office Northern Ireland**
Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast BT9 5RR
☎ 028 9025 2000 | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/searching-birth-marriage-and-death-records

> Do not rely on IrishGenealogy.ie for County Antrim — that site focuses on Cork, Kerry, and Dublin. Use GRONI or Ancestry/FindMyPast GRO collections for Northern Ireland events.

---

## Land, Probate & Other Records

| Record Type | Where Held | URL / Address |
|---|---|---|
| **Registry of Deeds (from 1708)** | PRAI, Henrietta Street, Dublin D01 K272 | https://www.prai.ie/ ; indexes at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/registry-of-deeds |
| **Pre-1858 Wills (Connor Diocese)** | National Archives Ireland (indexes; originals largely lost 1922) | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/ |
| **Post-1858 Wills (Belfast Registry)** | PRONI | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast |
| **Estate papers (north Antrim landlords)** | PRONI (mostly physical; some catalogued) | eCATALOGUE above |
| **School registers (from 1832)** | PRONI | eCATALOGUE above |
| **Ordnance Survey Memoirs (c. 1830s)** | PRONI; QUB Library; published by Institute of Irish Studies | Physical only |

---

## Key Repository Summary

| Repository | Address / URL |
|---|---|
| PRONI | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast BT3 9HQ · https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/services/proni-online-public-access |
| RCB Library | Braemor Park, Dublin 14 · https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy |
| National Archives Ireland | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 · https://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| GRONI | Colby House, Belfast BT9 5RR · https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/searching-birth-marriage-and-death-records |
| Linen Hall Library (newspapers) | 17 Donegall Square North, Belfast BT1 5GB · https://www.linenhall.com/ |
| NLI (Catholic registers) | https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| FamilySearch | https://www.familysearch.org |
| British Newspaper Archive (*Coleraine Chronicle*, *Northern Whig*) | https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 PRO fire (Dublin):** Destroyed roughly two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers held there, plus original census returns for 1861–1891 and many wills. Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Abstracts (FindMyPast) are the principal substitutes for lost records.
- **Irish censuses 1861–1891:** Deliberately destroyed by government order.
- **1821–1851 censuses:** Survive only in fragments used in old-age pension claims.

---

## Top 5 Action Steps

1. **Download PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF** → look up Billy parish → note microfilm numbers for every denomination before searching any online index.
2. **Search all five former union parishes together** (Billy, Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) — a family on any boundary may be registered in a neighbouring parish.
3. **NLI free Catholic registers** (https://registers.nli.ie/) — search under "Coleraine" (the relevant district of Diocese of Connor).
4. **Tithe Applotment Books + Griffith's Valuation** — together they name virtually every householder 1823–1864 and bracket the Famine.
5. **RootsIreland subscription** (http://www.rootsireland.ie/) — the most targeted Ulster-specific index for County Antrim church registers.
