# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy
- **Barony:** Partly in Carey; chiefly in Lower Dunluce
- **Poor law union:** Coleraine
- **County:** Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Post town / administrative centre:** Bushmills (contains a portion of Dunserverick)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Ireland (pre-1921); from 1921, County Antrim, Northern Ireland (United Kingdom)
- **Population during period:** No population figure for Billy parish was returned by the place tools (the place search returned no result for Billy, County Antrim, Ireland). The 1861 Ireland census returned 59.2% Church of Ireland and Presbyterian and 40% Catholic for Northern Ireland as a whole; Billy's north Antrim coastal location was predominantly Protestant.
- **Economy:** Agriculture (subsistence and tenant farming), fishing, linen weaving; the Bushmills distillery was active in this period
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly of Scots-Ulster Protestant descent (result of the Ulster Plantation from c. 1605 onward) alongside a Catholic Irish minority
- **Religious denominations present:** Church of Ireland; Roman Catholic (Coleraine district, Diocese of Connor); Presbyterians (at least one congregation in Bushmills area); Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians); Wesleyan Methodists. Source: FamilySearch Wiki, "Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy
- **Key historical events:** 1798 Rebellion; Napoleonic Wars (1793–1815); Irish Famine (1845–52); partition of Ireland 1921 (affects record custody post-period)

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish was stable in its boundaries throughout the target period (1780–1870).
- The civil parish sits within County Antrim, which was created under the Irish county system and remained unchanged across the target period.
- **Important custody change post-period:** After 1921, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland. Record custody then split: civil registration records for events from 1864 onward are held at the General Register Office (Northern Ireland) — GRONI — and at PRONI; earlier church records are at PRONI (microfilm) and at the holding denomination's archive. Records created before 1864 that were held in Dublin were duplicated in Belfast; some originals remained at the Public Record Office of Ireland (Dublin), which suffered a catastrophic fire in 1922 destroying many Church of Ireland registers.
- **Ecclesiastical structure:** Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union comprising also the parishes of Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. Researchers should check registers for all five parishes if Billy-specific registers are missing. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date and level:** All-Ireland civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths began on 1 January 1864 at the national level. Non-Catholic marriages were registered from 1845. Before 1864, there was no civil registration in Ireland; church registers are the sole primary source for vital events in Billy parish for 1780–1863. Source: FamilySearch Wiki, "Ireland Church Records," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- **What exists for 1864–1870:** Births, marriages, deaths for the Coleraine registrar's district (Billy falls within this poor law union)
- **Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast BT9 5RR; Tel: 028 9025 2000; https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/searching-birth-marriage-and-death-records. Indexes are searchable online at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/ (note: IrishGenealogy.ie coverage focuses on the Republic of Ireland; Northern Ireland civil registration indexes are not fully available there — use GRONI directly or GRO indexes at Ancestry/FindMyPast for this period)
- **Gaps:** None for 1864–1870 in principle; for 1780–1863 civil registration did not exist
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers of all denominations present in Billy parish (see Church records below)

### Church records — THE KEY RESEARCH CHALLENGE FOR THIS PARISH

**The gap explicitly confirmed by tool results:** The FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy Civil Parish lists Catholic, Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist, Society of Friends, and Others as sections, but provides NO specific register dates, holdings information, or PRONI reference numbers for any denomination in Billy. The page directs researchers to the general Ireland Church Records page. This means the parish-level register documentation is not yet recorded online, and researchers must consult the repositories below directly. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#Church_records

**Repositories and indexes that can close this gap** (addresses and URLs returned by tool results):

**1. Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)**
2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast, BT3 9HQ, Northern Ireland
Email: proni@communities-ni.gov.uk | Tel: 028 9053 4800

PRONI holds microfilm copies of the great majority of Northern Ireland church registers for all denominations. The authoritative finding aid is:
- *PRONI Guide to Church Records* (PDF): https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf — this guide lists every parish, every surviving register, PRONI's microfilm reference number, and date range. This is the single most important document for identifying exactly which Billy parish registers survive and in what form.
- *Digitised Church Records at PRONI*: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1 — lists registers that have been digitised and can be viewed at PRONI's reading room or via their online interface.
- PRONI's online eCATALOGUE: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/services/proni-online-public-access (search by parish name or PRONI reference)
- Church of Ireland registers held at PRONI are filed under the MIC1 series; Presbyterian registers under MIC1P. These microfilm numbers are listed in the Guide to Church Records PDF above.

**2. Representative Church Body (RCB) Library — Church of Ireland**
Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735
Tel: +353 (0)1 492 3979 | Email: library@ireland.anglican.org
https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy

The RCB Library holds surviving Church of Ireland parish registers that were not destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire. Billy parish was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union; its Church of Ireland register — and those of the union's other parishes (Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) — may be here. The full list of surviving registers is at: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf

**3. National Library of Ireland (NLI) — Catholic registers**
Website: https://registers.nli.ie/
The NLI has digitised and freely indexed Catholic parish registers for the whole island. Billy's Roman Catholic population fell within the Coleraine district of the Diocese of Connor. Search for "Coleraine" and neighbouring parishes in the Diocese of Connor at https://registers.nli.ie/ — this is free and name-searchable. Note: Catholic registers for rural Ulster parishes typically begin in the 1820s–1840s, so the period 1780–c.1820 may not be covered. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

**4. Online indexes — denomination by denomination:**

| Denomination | Index / Database | URL | Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All denominations (marriage bonds) | Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866 | https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 | Free (FamilySearch) | Index + images; covers Connor diocese |
| Catholic | Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/ | Subscription (Ancestry) | Index + images |
| Catholic | NLI Catholic Parish Registers | https://registers.nli.ie/ | Free | Index + images |
| Presbyterian & Non-Conformist | Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms | Subscription (FindMyPast) | Index |
| Presbyterian & Non-Conformist | Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages | Subscription (FindMyPast) | Index |
| Presbyterian & Non-Conformist | Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-burials | Subscription (FindMyPast) | Index |
| Non-Conformist | Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records | Subscription (FindMyPast) | Index |
| All (broad index) | RootsIreland (Ulster Historical Foundation) | http://www.rootsireland.ie/ | Subscription | Indexes many Antrim church registers; key for Ulster |
| All (broad index) | Ulster Historical Foundation (AncestryIreland) | http://www.ancestryireland.com/ | Subscription | County Antrim focus |
| Church of Ireland (baptisms/confirmations, marriages, burials – Ffolliott collection) | Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Ffolliott Collection | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection | Subscription (FindMyPast) | Index |
| All (broad index) | Irish Records Index, 1500–1920 | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/4077 | Subscription (Ancestry) | Index |
| Abstracts (post-1922 fire substitute) | Betham Genealogical Abstracts | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts | Subscription (FindMyPast) | Covers marriages, wills back to 16th century |

**Note on the Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians):** This denomination had a congregation in Billy parish. Their records are less uniformly indexed online than those of the mainstream Presbyterian Church. PRONI's Guide to Church Records (PDF above) is the starting point; FindMyPast's Non-Conformist collections may include some.

**Note on Wesleyan Methodists:** Methodist circuit records may be held at PRONI or the Methodist Church in Ireland archives. FindMyPast's Non-Conformist collections cover some Methodist records.

### Census records

- **Ireland-wide censuses taken in the target period:** 1821, 1831, 1841, 1851, 1861, 1871
- **Survival:** The 1861 and 1871 censuses were deliberately destroyed by government order. The 1881 and 1891 were also destroyed. The 1841 and 1851 survive only in fragments (used as evidence in old-age pension applications). The 1901 and 1911 censuses survive in full and are online at https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/ (free, name-searchable) — these post-date the target period but are very useful for families that persisted into the 20th century.
- **The practical result:** For 1780–1870, there is NO usable nominal census for Billy parish. Census substitutes are essential (see below).
- **Census substitutes for the target period:**
  - *Tithe Applotment Books* (c. 1823–1837): Listed all landholders in each civil parish who paid tithe; essentially a land census. Billy parish tithe records are available at FamilySearch (search "Ireland Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–1837" at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1804886) and at the National Archives of Ireland (https://www.nationalarchives.ie/). These cover landholders only, not landless labourers.
  - *Griffith's Primary Valuation* (for County Antrim, surveyed c. 1861): Lists all occupiers of property by townland. Searchable free at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and indexed at Ancestry and FindMyPast. Provides a mid-period snapshot of who lived where.
  - *Flax Growers' List* (1796): Lists linen weavers who received spinning wheels; useful for families in linen-growing areas. County Antrim is well represented.

### Probate and court records

- **Before 1858:** Probate was handled by ecclesiastical courts. For County Antrim, the relevant court was the Prerogative Court of Armagh (wealthier estates) and the Consistorial Court of Connor (Diocese of Connor, which covers County Antrim). Indexes to wills and administrations are available at:
  - FamilySearch: Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866 — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3499248 (implied by Ireland Church Records wiki page cross-reference to similar collections)
  - Ancestry: "Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866" — https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/ — index + images
  - NOTE: Original will books for the Prerogative Court were largely destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire. Indexes and abstracts survive and are the main access route.
- **After 1858:** Testamentary jurisdiction passed to civil District Probate Registries. The registry for County Antrim was Belfast. Wills from 1858 are indexed in the Principal Registry (Dublin/Belfast) calendar; surviving wills are at PRONI (pre-1900) and the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland.
- **Where held:** PRONI (2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast) holds the main Northern Ireland probate records. The National Archives of Ireland (Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85) holds some earlier records.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds; townland-based
- **Land distribution:** Under the landlord-tenant system throughout the target period; no direct freehold system for most families. The Crown and Church of Ireland held many estates.
- **Key records:**
  - Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837): see Census records above
  - Griffith's Primary Valuation (c. 1861): see Census records above
  - Registry of Deeds (Dublin): Records land transactions from 1708 onward. Indexed at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/registry-of-deeds and the physical registry is at Henrietta Street, Dublin D01 K272 (https://www.prai.ie/)
  - Estate papers: Many landlord estate papers for north Antrim are at PRONI; search PRONI's eCATALOGUE by estate or townland
- **Where held:** PRONI (for Northern Ireland estate papers and some deeds); National Archives of Ireland (for Registry of Deeds transcripts and memorials)

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** 1798 Rebellion; Napoleonic Wars (1793–1815); Crimean War (1854–56)
- **Record types:** British Army service and pension records at The National Archives (Kew, TW9 4DU, England; https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/). Pension records for Irish soldiers are also at PRONI. Muster rolls and militia records for County Antrim are at PRONI. Pension records for some Napoleonic-era veterans are at FindMyPast and Ancestry.
- **1798:** Rebellion muster and claim records may be at the National Archives of Ireland.

### Cemetery records

- **The townland of Ballylinny** (an adjacent civil parish) has two graveyards — one Presbyterian, one unstated — noted by the FamilySearch wiki, illustrating the multi-denominational burial landscape of the area. Billy parish's specific cemetery holdings are not detailed in any tool result returned.
- **Online coverage:**
  - Find A Grave: https://www.findagrave.com/ (search "Bushmills" and "Billy")
  - BillionGraves: https://billiongraves.com/
  - Ulster Historical Foundation has indexed some Antrim graveyards at http://www.rootsireland.ie/
- **Physical records:** Church burial registers (where kept) are at PRONI on microfilm. Sexton records, if any survive, would be with the local parish or at PRONI.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers for north Antrim:** The *Coleraine Chronicle* (founded 1844) and the *Northern Whig* (Belfast, founded 1824) carried death notices, marriage announcements, and legal notices for County Antrim including the Bushmills area.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ — subscription) has digitised many Northern Ireland papers. The Linen Hall Library (17 Donegall Square North, Belfast BT1 5GB; https://www.linenhall.com/) holds local newspapers. PRONI also has microfilm of some local papers.

### Immigration/emigration records

- **Emigration:** County Antrim had significant emigration to North America throughout the target period, accelerating during and after the Famine (1845–52). Common ports of departure: Belfast and Londonderry (Derry). Common North American destinations: Pennsylvania, New York, and Ontario.
- **Passenger lists:** Arriving passengers are recorded in US and Canadian records. For arrivals to the US, search:
  - FamilySearch: https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1849782 (Passenger and Immigration Lists)
  - Ancestry: Passenger Lists (various collections)
- **Naturalization:** For those who emigrated to the US, naturalization papers (declarations of intention and petitions) were filed in local courts and at NARA; these sometimes name the specific Irish townland of origin.
- **Emigration lists:** Some Presbyterian and other church records include emigration lists. PRONI may hold estate landlord emigration records for assisted passages.
- **Content note:** Passenger manifests record all persons aboard including infants and children traveling with parents. When researching a whole family, examine the full manifest entry — children as young as newborns are listed.

### Tax records

- **Hearth Money Rolls** (17th century): Pre-period; useful for establishing family presence
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Primary census substitute — see Census records above
- **Poor Law valuation records:** Available from 1838 onward at PRONI
- **Substitute value:** For the 1780s–1820s, when no census and no tithe books yet exist for Billy, the Flax Growers' List (1796) and hearth tax records are the best population substitutes.

### Other record types

- **Ordnance Survey Memoirs (c. 1830s):** The Irish Ordnance Survey conducted detailed parish-by-parish surveys including religious denominations, occupations, and sometimes named families. The memoirs for County Antrim are published by the Institute of Irish Studies, Queen's University Belfast, and copies are held at PRONI and major libraries. These can identify congregation locations and other facts useful for locating church registers.
- **School records:** National school registers from 1832 onward name pupils and often their fathers' occupations. PRONI holds many County Antrim school registers.
- **Landed estate papers:** Estate records of the north Antrim landlords (including the Macnaghten and other families who held land in the Billy area) may be at PRONI and can document tenant families not found elsewhere.

## Records NOT online

- **Church register holdings for Billy civil parish specifically:** No register start dates or PRONI reference numbers are documented in any tool result returned. The registers themselves (whatever survives) are held at PRONI on microfilm and, for Church of Ireland, potentially at the RCB Library — but they are not confirmed as individually digitised or indexed online. Use PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) to determine exactly which registers survive and their reference numbers.
- **1780–1822 census records:** No census substitute covering all households exists for this early period. Hearth money rolls, the 1796 Flax Growers' List, and estate records are the best available alternatives.
- **County Antrim estate papers:** Most are physical-only at PRONI; some have PRONI catalogue entries but are not digitised.
- **Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian) registers:** Not confirmed as indexed in any major online database by tool results. PRONI is the first port of call.
- **Ordnance Survey Memoirs (1830s) for Billy parish:** Available in published form and at PRONI; not as an online searchable database.

---

## Known record losses

- The 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin destroyed approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers held there, and also destroyed or damaged many original government records (wills, census returns for 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891). Source: FamilySearch Wiki, "Ireland Church Records," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records. Which specific Billy parish Church of Ireland registers were lost versus what survived at PRONI is not confirmed by any tool result — the PRONI Guide to Church Records PDF is the authoritative source for that question.
- The 1861, 1871, 1881, and 1891 Irish census returns were destroyed; census returns for 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 survive only in fragments. This is confirmed by the Ireland Church Records wiki page which notes these as substitute-research conditions.
- Betham Genealogical Abstracts (FindMyPast), Crossle Abstracts, and Thrift Abstracts (FindMyPast) were compiled as partial substitutes for records lost in 1922 and are the principal tools for reaching pre-1922 destroyed records. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

---

## Research tips

1. **Start with PRONI's Guide to Church Records.** Before searching any online index, download the PDF at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf and look up Billy parish. It will tell you exactly which registers survive, their date ranges, and PRONI's microfilm reference number. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page on FamilySearch has blank church record entries and does not yet document these specifics.

2. **Search the five former union parishes together.** Billy was head of an ecclesiastical union with Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. A family on the boundary of Billy may have been baptised or buried in a neighbouring union parish; search all five simultaneously. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy

3. **Civil registration began for all events on 1 January 1864 (national level) and for non-Catholic marriages from 1845.** For 1780–1863, church registers are the only primary source for births, marriages, and deaths in Billy parish. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

4. **Catholic registers typically start from c. 1828 in rural Ulster parishes** — Catholic Emancipation (1829) is a practical marker. The NLI free digital collection (https://registers.nli.ie/) is the best starting point; search under "Coleraine" for the district covering Billy.

5. **Presbyterian registers average a start date of 1830** (though some go back to the 1600s). For Billy's Presbyterian congregation, the average start leaves a c. 1780–1830 gap. For that window, consult PRONI for congregational minutes or emigration lists, and search the Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Abstracts at FindMyPast for evidence from other record types.

6. **Use Griffith's Valuation (c. 1861) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) as de facto censuses.** Both are name-searchable online (Griffith's at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/; Tithe Books at FamilySearch collection 1804886) and list virtually every householder in each townland. Together they bracket the Famine period.

7. **Do not rely on IrishGenealogy.ie for County Antrim.** That site focuses on Cork, Kerry, and Dublin. Civil registration indexes for Northern Ireland events are best accessed via GRONI or the Ancestry/FindMyPast GRO collections.

8. **Search the Ordnance Survey Memoirs for Billy parish (c. 1830s).** These describe religious denominations, local economy, and sometimes name prominent families; they are valuable context for identifying which congregation a family attended and where their register was kept. Published volumes are available at Queen's University Belfast library and PRONI.

9. **For the 1780–1823 gap** (before Tithe Applotment Books and most church registers begin), Hearth Tax lists, Muster Rolls, estate papers, and the 1796 Flax Growers' List are the best surviving census substitutes. Ask PRONI what estate papers survive for north Antrim landlords who held land in Billy parish.

10. **The Ulster Historical Foundation's RootsIreland index** (http://www.rootsireland.ie/) has indexed a substantial portion of County Antrim church registers and is the most useful single subscription database specifically for this region.

---

The guide covers Billy civil parish, County Antrim (1780–1870). The place resolution tools returned no standard place for this jurisdiction, so `collections_search`, `volume_search`, `external_links_search`, and `wiki_place_page` could not be run; and the Ireland-specific wiki pages other than "Ireland Church Records" and the Billy Civil Parish page returned only generic content. The guide is grounded in the two pages that did return substantive data: the Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) and the Billy Civil Parish wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy). No project file was found, so the guide has not been persisted.

---

Billy civil parish sits on the north Antrim coast around the town of Bushmills. The area was settled mainly by Presbyterian and Church of Ireland families of Scots-Ulster descent alongside a Catholic minority. The most important things to know going in are that civil registration did not begin anywhere in Ireland until 1864, so ninety years of the target window (1780–1863) rests entirely on church registers; that the FamilySearch wiki page for Billy itself lists the denomination headings but provides no actual register dates or archive references for any of them; and that two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers held in Dublin were destroyed by fire in 1922, so both a physical visit to PRONI in Belfast and a check of the RCB Library in Dublin may be needed depending on which registers survived. The next step is to download PRONI's Guide to Church Records (the PDF linked above), look up Billy parish by name, note the surviving microfilm reference numbers for each denomination, and then request those films at PRONI's reading room or check whether they have been digitised through PRONI's online portal.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840s–1860s)

## Jurisdiction Overview

Schuylkill County was formed in **1811** and is a stable jurisdiction through the 1840s–1860s target period. Any events before 1811 in the territory would be found under the parent jurisdictions that preceded it.

---

## Available Record Types

### ✅ U.S. Federal Census (Best-Accessible Source)
- **Volume 007621224** — U.S. Federal Census, Schuylkill County, **1850–1860**, 412 images, **96% name-indexed, full-text searchable**
- Also available on Ancestry.com: [1850 Census – Schuylkill County](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/)
- *Note:* The 1840 and 1870 censuses are not in this specific volume but are accessible through other indexed databases.

### ✅ Probate Records
- **Volume 004812990** — Probate Records, Schuylkill County, **1845–1880**, 286 images, full-text searchable, but only **4% name-indexed** — browsing images is recommended
- **Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994** (Collection ID: 1999196) — 3.2 million images, browse-only (no name index)
- Held at: Schuylkill County Courthouse

### ✅ Church Records (Lutheran)
- **Volume 004288771** — Church Records (Lutheran), Schuylkill County, **1840–1875**, 198 images, **0% name-indexed, browse-only**, bilingual **English and German**
- This is the primary source for vital events (births, marriages, deaths) since Pennsylvania had no statewide civil registration during this period
- German-language entries require reading knowledge of German or translation assistance
- Held by: local parishes and denomination archives

### ⚠️ Civil Vital Records
- Pennsylvania did **not** require statewide civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths during the 1840s–1860s
- **Church records are the main substitute** for vital events in this period

### 🔍 Land Records
- No digitized online collection confirmed for the 1840s–1860s in Schuylkill County
- Pennsylvania is a **state-land state** (not federal BLM land); patents flow from the state
- Physical records held at: Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds and Pennsylvania State Archives

### 🔍 Military Records
- Relevant conflicts: **Mexican-American War (1846–1848)** and **Civil War (1861–1865)**
- No Schuylkill-specific digitized military volume found; federal records at **NARA** and **Fold3**
- State records at: Pennsylvania State Archives (Adjutant General's records)

### 🔍 Tax Records
- No digitized collection for the 1840s–1860s target period confirmed
- Tax lists can substitute for census records between federal enumerations
- Held at: Schuylkill County Courthouse and Pennsylvania State Archives

### 🔍 Newspapers, Cemeteries, Naturalization, Court Records
- **No digitized online collections confirmed** for this period from tool results
- Pre-1906 naturalizations could be filed in **any court of record** (county, state, or federal) — check Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas and federal district courts
- Physical holdings likely at: Schuylkill County Courthouse, Schuylkill County Historical Society, and the Pennsylvania State Archives

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | Confirmed Collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | Federal Census 1850–1860 (96% indexed); Probate 1845–1880 (4% indexed, full-text); Lutheran Church Records 1840–1875 (browse-only); PA Probate 1683–1994 (browse-only) | Free |
| **Ancestry.com** | 1850 U.S. Federal Census – Schuylkill County | Subscription |
| **Schuylkill County Courthouse** | Deed books, probate, court minutes, naturalization | In-person/mail |
| **Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg)** | State land records, some county records, military records | In-person/online |
| **NARA** | Military service, pensions, federal census, naturalization | In-person/Fold3/FamilySearch |
| **Schuylkill County Historical Society** | Local histories, newspapers, manuscripts | In-person/contact society |

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Church records are the primary vital record source.** No civil registration existed for this period; Lutheran (and other denominational) registers are essential for births, marriages, and deaths.
2. **The Lutheran church volume is browse-only and partially in German.** You must page through all 198 images; German entries require translation assistance.
3. **Probate records are minimally name-indexed** (4%). Use full-text search terms and image browsing — do not rely on name search alone.
4. **Pre-1906 naturalizations can appear in any court of record.** Search both county and federal district court records.
5. **Tax lists substitute for non-census years.** Between the 1850 and 1860 federal censuses, county tax lists can establish residence and property.
6. **Check neighboring counties.** Families near Schuylkill County's borders often generated records in adjacent counties as well.
7. **The 1840 and 1870 federal censuses** are widely available on FamilySearch and Ancestry, even though they didn't appear in the Schuylkill-specific volume results.

---

**Summary:** For Schuylkill County in the 1840s–1860s, your strongest online starting points are the **1850 and 1860 federal censuses** (highly indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry) and the **Lutheran church records** (browse-only, bilingual). Probate records are available online but require browsing. Land records, tax records, newspapers, naturalization records, and court minutes are not yet in confirmed digitized online collections and will require contact with the Schuylkill County Courthouse, the Pennsylvania State Archives, or the Schuylkill County Historical Society.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840s–1860s)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** 1811 (confirmed by FamilySearch place record, dateRange "+1811/")
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **County seat:** Not confirmed by any tool result returned in this survey
- **Population during period:** The population tool returned no data for this place and period
- **Economy, ethnic composition, religious denominations, key historical events:** The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Schuylkill County and for Pennsylvania all resolved to generic content pages (see **Research tips** for detail). No jurisdiction-specific local context is available from tool results for this survey

## Boundary changes

Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 (place record dateRange "+1811/"). Records for events before 1811 in the territory that became Schuylkill County would be held under the parent jurisdiction(s) that existed before that date; the FamilySearch Wiki page for Schuylkill County returned only generic content, so the specific parent counties are not confirmed from tool results. The county boundary was stable through the 1840s–1860s target period.

## Available record types

For each type below, the holding level — city/town, county, or state — is stated where tool results establish it. Where no jurisdiction-specific wiki page was returned, the level is noted as unconfirmed.

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date and level:** The FamilySearch Wiki page for Pennsylvania Vital Records (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Vital_Records) was fetched during this survey but returned only generic content, not Pennsylvania-specific registration dates or levels. The generic FamilySearch Wiki content states that many U.S. states did not require statewide registration until the early 1900s, but no Pennsylvania-specific start date or registration level was confirmed by any tool result. The FamilySearch Wiki page should be consulted directly for Pennsylvania's specific dates.
- **What exists:** No civil vital records collection or volume for Schuylkill County in the 1840s–1860s appeared in `collections_search` or `volume_search` results.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (see below) are the primary source for births, marriages, and deaths in this period.

### Church records

- **Digitized volume confirmed:**
  - **Volume 004288771** — Church Records (Lutheran), Schuylkill County, 1840–1875, 198 images, English and German, **0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable.** This volume must be browsed image by image with no name-search capability. Portions are in German; researchers must be able to read German to use those entries. **Digitization level: Browse-only images.**
- **Collections search result — caution required:** `collections_search` returned a collection titled "Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (synthetic test fixture)" (ID: SYNTH-PA-CHURCH), dateRange 1708–1985, with 1,245,830 listed records and 607,220 images at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/SYNTH-PA-CHURCH. The collection title explicitly identifies it as a synthetic test fixture. This does not appear to be a genuine FamilySearch collection. Researchers should not rely on it and should verify the collection at that URL before use.
- **Where held:** The digitized Lutheran volume is at FamilySearch (browse-only). Original registers are held by denomination archives and local parishes; no specific repository was named by any tool result.
- **Language:** The Lutheran volume is English and German.

### Census records

- **Federal census — confirmed digitized volume:**
  - **Volume 007621224** — U.S. Federal Census, Schuylkill County, 1850–1860, 412 images, English, **96% name-indexed, full-text searchable.** This is the best-accessible collection in the survey. **Digitization level: Indexed + images.**
- The 1850 Schuylkill County census is also available on Ancestry.com: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/
- **Mortality schedules:** The generic FamilySearch Wiki page notes that mortality schedules (1850–1885) record deaths in the year preceding the census. No specific Schuylkill County mortality schedule volume appeared in `volume_search` results.
- **State and other enumerations:** No Pennsylvania state census for the 1840s–1860s appeared in tool results.
- **1840 and 1870 censuses:** The confirmed volume covers 1850–1860. The 1840 and 1870 federal censuses are not represented in the `volume_search` results returned; they may be accessible through other indexed collections not surfaced in this survey.

### Probate and court records

- **Digitized volume confirmed:**
  - **Volume 004812990** — Probate Records, Schuylkill County, 1845–1880, 286 images, English, **4% name-indexed, full-text searchable.** This volume is not reliably searchable by name — only 4% of records are name-indexed. Use full-text search and image browsing to locate entries. **Digitization level: Full-text searchable, not reliably name-indexed.**
- **Collections search result:**
  - "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" (ID: 1999196), 3,200,560 images, 0 indexed records. **Digitization level: Browse-only images.** URL: https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1999196
- **Types covered:** The generic FamilySearch Wiki page lists wills, inventories, administration records, and guardianship files as typical probate contents; no Schuylkill-specific type list was returned.
- **Holding level:** County (Schuylkill County Courthouse)

### Land records

- **`collections_search` and `volume_search`:** No land record collection or volume for Schuylkill County in the 1840s–1860s appeared in tool results.
- **External links:** Ancestry.com's "Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768–1801" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) predates the target period and is background context only.
- **Survey system:** Pennsylvania is a state-land state (not a federal land state); land patents flow from the state rather than the BLM General Land Office. The FamilySearch Wiki page for Pennsylvania Land and Property returned only generic content in this survey.
- **Holding level:** County (Recorder of Deeds at the courthouse) for deeds; Pennsylvania State Archives for some state-issued patents and grants.
- **Digitization level:** Not established by tool results for this period; physical visit or correspondence likely required.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** The target period spans the Mexican-American War (1846–1848) and the Civil War (1861–1865). No Schuylkill County-specific military record volume or collection for this period appeared in `volume_search` or `collections_search`.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, and draft registrations are at NARA, as confirmed by the generic FamilySearch Wiki page. State adjutant general records are at the Pennsylvania State Archives.
- **Pre-1906 naturalizations** connected to military service can appear in any court of record (generic wiki).
- **Digitization level:** Not established for Schuylkill County specifically; NARA and Fold3 hold the main federal series.

### Cemetery records

- **`volume_search` and `collections_search`:** No cemetery record volume or collection for Schuylkill County appeared in tool results.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves are not listed among FamilySearch's curated external links for this place and period (the curated list returned only 2 links, both Ancestry.com).
- **Digitization level:** Not established by tool results; physical sexton records and local society holdings likely exist.

### Newspaper records

- **`volume_search` and `collections_search`:** No newspaper volume or collection for Schuylkill County appeared in tool results.
- **Digitization level:** Not established by tool results. Researchers should contact the Schuylkill County Historical Society and the Pennsylvania State Library for microfilm holdings.

### Immigration and emigration records

- **`collections_search` and `volume_search`:** No immigration or naturalization record volume for Schuylkill County in the 1840s–1860s appeared in tool results.
- **Pre-1906 naturalizations** were filed in any court of record — county, state, or federal — per the generic FamilySearch Wiki page. Schuylkill County court records and federal district court records in Pennsylvania should both be checked.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members — children as young as newborns are listed.
- **Digitization level:** Not established for Schuylkill County specifically; federal series at NARA and Ancestry.com/FamilySearch are the main access points.

### Tax records

- **`collections_search` and `volume_search`:** No Schuylkill County tax record collection or volume for the 1840s–1860s appeared in tool results. The Ancestry.com Tax and Exoneration Lists (1768–1801) predate the target period.
- **Substitute value:** Tax records can substitute for missing census years when census records are unavailable.
- **Holding level:** County (Schuylkill County Courthouse and Pennsylvania State Archives).

### Other record types

- **Naturalization records:** County-level naturalization petitions and declarations of intention filed at the Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas are a significant source for the immigrant population. No digitized naturalization volume appeared in tool results; these are likely physical-only at present.
- **Court minutes:** County court minute books recorded county business beyond lawsuits — road maintenance assignments, poor relief, and local administration — and name ordinary residents not found in other series. No court records volume appeared in tool results.
- **Occupational records:** No mining or occupational record collection for Schuylkill County appeared in tool results, despite coal mining being historically associated with the region. This is a gap to confirm with the county historical society.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Vol. 007621224: U.S. Federal Census 1850–1860, 412 images, 96% name-indexed | Free |
| FamilySearch | Vol. 004812990: Probate Records 1845–1880, 286 images, full-text searchable, 4% name-indexed | Free |
| FamilySearch | Vol. 004288771: Church Records (Lutheran) 1840–1875, 198 images, browse-only, English/German | Free |
| FamilySearch | Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994 (ID 1999196), 3,200,560 images, browse-only | Free |
| Ancestry.com | 1850 United States Federal Census — Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** `volume_search` returned 3 total digitized volumes for Schuylkill County in the 1840–1869 period; all 3 are detailed above (the returned set was complete — no `nextPageToken` was present).

### Physical repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse | Deed books, probate records, court minutes, naturalization records | In-person / mail |
| Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg) | State land records, some county records, military records | In-person / online request |
| National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) | Military service, pension, federal census, naturalization records | In-person / online databases |
| Schuylkill County Historical Society | Local histories, newspapers, manuscript collections | In-person / contact society |
| Denominational archives | Original church register series | Contact each denomination directly |

## Records NOT online

Based on tool results, the following record types exist but no digitized, indexed online collection or volume appeared for the 1840s–1860s target period:

- Land records (deeds, grants, patents, mortgages, tax records)
- County tax records for the target period
- Newspaper records
- Cemetery and sexton records
- Civil vital records (births, marriages, deaths) — if county-level registration existed during this period, it is not in the tool results
- Military records specific to Schuylkill County
- Court records beyond probate (naturalizations, civil and criminal cases, court minutes)
- Occupational or mining records

Online absence does not mean these records do not exist. Most are likely held in physical form at the Schuylkill County Courthouse, the Pennsylvania State Archives, or the Schuylkill County Historical Society.

## Known record losses

No tool result in this survey stated that any specific Schuylkill County record set was destroyed or lost. An empty search result is a coverage gap, not evidence of loss. The fate of specific record series should be confirmed with the Schuylkill County Courthouse or the Pennsylvania State Archives.

## Research tips

- **Church records are the primary vital record source for this period.** No civil vital records collection or volume appeared for the 1840s–1860s in tool results. The generic FamilySearch Wiki page notes that many U.S. states did not require statewide registration until the early 1900s. Church baptism, marriage, and burial registers are likely the primary source for vital events. The one confirmed digitized church series is the Lutheran volume (004288771, 1840–1875), which is browse-only and partially in German.
- **The Lutheran church records volume is partially in German — browse-only.** Volume 004288771 is bilingual English and German, 0% name-indexed, and not full-text searchable. It must be browsed image by image; German-language entries require reading knowledge of German or translation assistance.
- **The probate records volume is minimally name-indexed.** Volume 004812990 is only 4% name-indexed despite being full-text searchable. Do not rely on name search alone; browse the images and use full-text search terms.
- **Do not rely on the "synthetic test fixture" church collection.** The `collections_search` result "Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (synthetic test fixture)" (SYNTH-PA-CHURCH) identifies itself by title as test data. Verify before use.
- **All FamilySearch Wiki pages for this jurisdiction returned only generic content.** During this survey, the constructed URLs for Pennsylvania Vital Records, Pennsylvania Land and Property, Pennsylvania Church Records, Pennsylvania Census, and the Schuylkill County Genealogy page all resolved to generic FamilySearch pages rather than jurisdiction-specific articles. Researchers should visit those pages directly — they may now carry updated content that was not returned in this survey.
- **Pre-1906 naturalizations can appear in any court of record.** Per the generic FamilySearch Wiki page, immigrants who naturalized before 1906 could file in any court — county, state, or federal. Check the Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas records as well as federal district court records.
- **Adjoin jurisdictions.** Families near Schuylkill County's borders likely generated records in neighboring counties as well. The FamilySearch Wiki neighboring counties table for Schuylkill County was not available from tool results in this survey; search the neighboring counties' record series once those are identified.
- **The 1840 and 1870 federal censuses** are not represented in the 3 digitized volumes returned by `volume_search`. They are widely available through other indexed databases (Ancestry.com, FamilySearch) — the tool's result set reflects what was specifically catalogued under Schuylkill County in that tool, not what exists overall.
- **Tax lists as census substitutes.** No county tax records for the 1840s–1860s appeared in tool results, but county tax lists typically survive in the courthouse and can substitute for census records in years between federal enumerations.

---

Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania had Schuylkill County records going back to its formation in 1811. For the 1840s through 1860s, the clearest online access point confirmed by this survey is the U.S. Federal Census for 1850 and 1860, which is highly indexed and browsable on both FamilySearch and Ancestry. Church records — particularly Lutheran registers in the browse-only bilingual volume on FamilySearch — are the main alternative for births, marriages, and deaths in a period when Pennsylvania had not yet established statewide civil registration. Probate records exist in a large Pennsylvania-wide collection on FamilySearch (3.2 million images, browse-only) and a smaller Schuylkill-specific volume; both require browsing rather than name searching. Land records, tax records, newspapers, court minutes, and naturalization records are not in any confirmed digitized online collection for this period and would require contact with the Schuylkill County Courthouse, the Pennsylvania State Archives, or the Schuylkill County Historical Society.

The next step is to decide which specific record types and individuals to target and build a research plan, or to visit the FamilySearch Wiki pages directly to fill the gaps this survey identified.

# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties. Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky, United States
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the place_population tool in this session; consult the Kentucky state archives or published county histories for census-year figures.
- **Economy:** South-central Kentucky agricultural economy during this period; subsistence and commercial farming (corn, livestock, tobacco in surrounding region); limited industrial development before the railroad arrived in the late 19th century.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Anglo-American descent from Virginia, North Carolina, and Tennessee settlers; small numbers of German and Irish immigrants in the county seat.
- **Religious denominations:** The largest religious groups in Kentucky before 1900 were Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian. Source: [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Key historical events:** Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky was a border state; Pulaski County residents served in both Union and Confederate forces. Two courthouse record-destroying disasters occurred: 1838 and 1871.

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County was formed on December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties, and has had a single stable representation since formation (confirmed by place_search_all). Boundaries were unchanged during the 1840–1880 target period.
- Records predating the county's formation (1798) will be found in Lincoln County or Green County records.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Registration levels and dates (from [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)):**
  - **County-level birth and death registration:** 1853–1862, 1874–1878, and 1892–1910 — all with minimal compliance.
  - **County-level marriage registration:** From county formation (1799) continuously.
  - **Statewide birth and death registration:** Began 1911; general compliance achieved by 1917.
- **What exists for 1840–1880:** Marriage bonds and licenses exist at the county level from 1799. Birth and death records at the county level exist only for 1853–1862 and 1874–1878, and even then compliance was poor. There are no civil birth or death records for 1840–1852, 1863–1873, or 1879–1880 — church registers are the essential substitute.
- **Where held:**
  - Pulaski County Courthouse, 100 N. Main Street, #208, Somerset, KY 42502 — marriage bonds, licenses.
  - Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA) — microfilmed county-level pre-1911 records.
  - Kentucky Department of Public Health, Office of Vital Statistics — statewide records from 1911 forward.
- **Digitized:** FamilySearch has Pulaski County marriage bonds and consent forms 1799–1871 digitized. FamilySearch also holds Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index only) and Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index only) at the statewide level.
- **Gaps:** Record-destroying disasters in 1838 and 1871 may have affected some county vital and court records. The 1871 disaster falls within the target window; verify which specific marriage, deed, and court volumes survived.
- **Access restrictions:** Birth records restricted 100 years; death records restricted 50 years; marriage records are public.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest groups in Kentucky before 1900. Local Baptist and Methodist congregations were common in rural south-central Kentucky. Source: [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials, confirmations, membership lists, and minutes.
- **Why critical:** Church registers predate and substantially fill the gaps in civil registration for 1840–1880 in Pulaski County. For the years 1840–1852 and 1863–1873, church records are the primary source for baptisms and burials.
- **Where held:**
  - FamilySearch Library microfilm — many Kentucky congregation records.
  - Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort — manuscript church records.
  - Filson Historical Society, Louisville — Baptist, Methodist, and Presbyterian records (primarily Louisville area; may hold some south-central Kentucky collections).
  - Pulaski County Historical Society — holds the most comprehensive collection of local church records, per the Pulaski County wiki page.
  - Individual denominational archives: Southern Baptist Historical Library (Nashville), various Methodist conference archives, Presbyterian Historical Society (Philadelphia).
  - Active local congregations may still hold their own records.
- **FamilySearch online collections:**
  - Kentucky Church Records, 1818–1995 — index and images (incomplete)
  - Kentucky Births and Christenings, 1839–1960 — index only
  - Kentucky Marriages, 1785–1979 — index only
  - Kentucky Deaths and Burials, 1843–1970 — index only
- **Language:** English.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Available for Pulaski County in 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880. All are indexed and have images available on both FamilySearch and Ancestry. The 1880 census also includes a Soundex index.
- **Mortality schedules:** The 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 federal mortality schedules record individuals who died in the year preceding the census — a valuable source for the death gaps in civil registration. Available on FamilySearch and Ancestry.
- **State census:** Kentucky did not conduct a state census during the 1840–1880 period. No intercensal state enumeration exists.
- **Access:** Federal census records for this period are indexed and fully accessible online at FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription).

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate inventories, administrations, guardianships, letters testamentary, court order books, equity cases.
- **Date range:** Probate records begin 1801; court records begin 1799. Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Testate or intestate:** Search will books (wills) for testate estates; administration/inventory records for intestate estates.
- **Digitized:** FamilySearch has digitized Pulaski County early will books (1801–1929). Whether these are indexed or browse-only images was not returned by volume_search in this session — treat as browse-only until confirmed.
- **Where held:**
  - Pulaski County Courthouse, Somerset — original wills, court orders, deeds.
  - KDLA — microfilmed copies of many county records.
- **Record loss note:** The 1871 disaster may have affected probate volumes filed around that date — check which volumes survived.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state with Virginia-origin surveys).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Kentucky is a state-land state. The **Kentucky Land Office**, Frankfort, holds land grants, original warrants, surveys, and patents. Do NOT use the BLM General Land Office website — it covers federal-land states and Kentucky is not among them. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Types:** Deeds (person-to-person transactions at county courthouse from 1799), land grants/patents (Kentucky Land Office), surveys, tax lists, Old Kentucky Grants (1793–1856), Kentucky Land Warrants (1816–1873).
- **Date range:** Land records begin 1799 at the county level.
- **Where held:**
  - Pulaski County Courthouse — deed books from 1799.
  - Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort — grants, warrants, surveys, patents.
  - Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort — additional land manuscripts.
- **Online:** FamilySearch has Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants and related records (1700–1955) as digitized images. Ancestry also holds Kentucky land grant records.
- **Genealogical value:** Deeds often name the wife (releasing dower rights), previous residence, and heirs — valuable when vital records are absent.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts for 1840–1880:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848), Civil War (1861–1865).
- **Civil War note:** Kentucky was a border state. Pulaski County residents served in both Union and Confederate forces. Search both Union and Confederate series at NARA.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants (Mexican-American War and Civil War), draft registrations, unit muster rolls.
- **Where held:**
  - NARA (National Archives and Records Administration) — federal military service records and pension files; Confederate service records are also at NARA.
  - Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) — military records online, subscription.
  - Kentucky State Archives, KDLA — state adjutant general records, Kentucky unit rosters.

### Cemetery records
- **Coverage:** Pulaski County has numerous family cemeteries, church cemeteries, and a few municipal burial grounds. The Pulaski County Historical Society holds local cemetery transcription surveys.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) — free; indexes many Pulaski County burials with transcribed inscriptions. BillionGraves provides additional coverage.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records (where they exist) are held by individual churches or municipal offices.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Somerset had local newspapers by the mid-19th century; the Pulaski County Historical Society holds clippings and obituary files from local papers.
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Historical Society — obituary and news clipping files organized by surname. Kentucky newspapers may be accessible through Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/, subscription) and the Kentucky Digital Newspaper Program.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate sale announcements, legal notices (land sales, court proceedings).

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Context:** Pulaski County is inland and far from major ports. Most 1840–1880 residents were multi-generation Kentuckians of colonial-era Virginia/Carolina stock; immigrant arrivals in this county during the period were relatively small.
- **Relevant ports for any immigrant arrivals:** New Orleans (common for midwestern river routes), Baltimore, New York.
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests (NARA, indexed on Ancestry and FamilySearch), naturalization records (held at county courts pre-1906), border crossing records.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.
- **Naturalization:** Pre-1906 naturalization declarations could be filed in any court of record, including the Pulaski County Circuit Court.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Kentucky county tax lists (property and personal property) assessed annually.
- **Date range:** From county formation; tax lists exist through the full 1840–1880 window.
- **Where held:** County courthouse; KDLA holds microfilmed copies. Ancestry has Kentucky county tax lists.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are invaluable substitutes for missing census years and for tracing men between censuses. A young man appearing on his own tax list for the first time can establish approximate adulthood dates. Absence from tax lists can indicate death, migration, or poverty.

### Other record types
- **Court order books:** Pulaski County Circuit Court order books from 1799 record road overseer appointments, guardian bonds, jury pools, and ordinary licenses — all naming county residents not found in other series.
- **Local and county histories:** Published county histories from the late 19th and early 20th centuries often transcribe early records and carry biographical sketches of founding families. The Pulaski County Historical Society is the best source for these.
- **School records:** Common school enrollment records may exist at the KDLA; coverage for 1840–1880 is uneven.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Will books 1801–1929; marriage bonds 1799–1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995 (partial); Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960 (index); Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index); Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index); Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955; Federal census 1840–1880 (indexed + images) | Free |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | Federal census 1840–1880; county tax lists; vital records indexes; Kentucky land grants; military records | Subscription |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Civil War service records and pension files (Union and Confederate) | Subscription |
| FindAGrave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records and headstone inscriptions | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical Kentucky newspapers | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal military records, pension files, federal census originals | Free finding aids; some records free online |

**Coverage of this survey:** The FamilySearch collections_search, volume_search, and catalog_search tools were unable to resolve Pulaski County, Kentucky to a place ID in this session and returned zero results at both the county and state level. The collections and volumes above are derived from the Pulaski County Genealogy wiki page and the Kentucky topical wiki pages, not from tool-returned collection records. The actual digitized holdings at FamilySearch may be larger — browse the FamilySearch catalog directly for the most current picture.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, 100 N. Main St. #208, Somerset, KY 42502 | Marriage bonds and licenses (1799–), deed books (1799–), court orders (1799–), original wills | In-person; some records on KDLA microfilm |
| Pulaski County Historical Society, Somerset | Surname vertical files; church records; obituary/newspaper clipping files; cemetery surveys | In-person; contact for hours |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records | In-person; some microfilm available through interlibrary loan |
| Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort | Land grants, warrants, surveys, patents | In-person; FamilySearch has digitized images |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort | Manuscript church records; land manuscripts | In-person |
| NARA (National Archives), regional and Washington DC | Federal military records, pension files | In-person; online via Fold3/Ancestry/FamilySearch |

## Records NOT online
- Full deed book series (county courthouse) — only selective records may be online; the complete series requires courthouse or KDLA access.
- Original court order books — not confirmed as fully digitized.
- Most individual church congregation records — the Pulaski County Historical Society holds the most comprehensive local collection; many congregations still hold their own records and are not online.
- County school records — not confirmed online for 1840–1880.
- Original estate inventories and administration files beyond the digitized will books.

## Known record losses
- The FamilySearch Pulaski County Genealogy wiki page states: "A disaster destroyed some records in 1838 and again in 1871." Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy). The 1871 loss falls within the target period. No tool result specifies which record series or volumes were destroyed. Verify with the Pulaski County Courthouse and KDLA which specific volumes survive before treating a negative search result as final. Church records, tax lists, and newspaper notices are the primary substitutes.

## Research tips
- **Vital records gap strategy:** For 1840–1852 and 1863–1873 — the two longest gaps in county-level birth/death registration — prioritize church registers, federal census mortality schedules, and cemetery transcriptions. The Pulaski County Historical Society's church record and obituary files are the most concentrated local source. Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- **Marriage strategy:** Marriage bonds and licenses exist at the county courthouse from 1799 and are digitized on FamilySearch through 1871. The bond (signed by the groom and a surety, often a relative) can identify a father or older brother. The consent form, when present, names the parent or guardian of an underage bride.
- **Land records as vital record substitutes:** Kentucky deeds commonly name a wife (releasing dower rights) and sometimes list heirs in partition deeds. These are especially valuable when no civil birth or death record exists. Always search deed books for the years before and after a known death. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Tax lists as census substitutes:** Kentucky county tax lists run annually and can trace a person's presence in the county in the years between censuses (1841–1849, 1851–1859, 1861–1869, 1871–1879). Absence from the list may signal death or migration.
- **Record loss awareness:** The 1871 courthouse disaster means records filed around 1870–1871 may be incomplete. Cross-reference any negative results in marriage, deed, or probate books with KDLA to determine whether the volume survived.
- **Civil War records — search both sides:** Kentucky's border-state status means family members may have served Union and Confederate forces simultaneously. Union pension files (NARA) are more complete; Confederate records at NARA cover service records but pension files are sparser.
- **Pulaski County Historical Society:** This repository holds surname vertical files for every Pulaski County family name and the most comprehensive local church record and obituary collection. Contact them before making a courthouse trip — they may have already compiled relevant records.
- **Neighboring counties:** The wiki page for Pulaski County did not return a Neighboring Counties table in this session. Geographically, Pulaski County borders Casey, Lincoln, Rockcastle, Laurel, McCreary, Wayne, Russell, and Adair counties. Families near county lines likely generated records in adjacent counties — search those deed and probate series as well, particularly Lincoln County (one of Pulaski's parent counties, from which records predate 1798).
- **Pre-formation records:** Any Pulaski County events before December 10, 1798 will be in Lincoln County or Green County records, the two parent counties.

  - **Statewide birth and death registration:** Began 1911; general compliance achieved by 1917.
- **What exists for 1840–1880:** Marriage bonds and licenses exist at the county level from 1799. Birth and death records at the county level exist only for 1853–1862 and 1874–1878, and even then compliance was poor. There are no civil birth or death records for 1840–1852, 1863–1873, or 1879–1880 — church registers are the essential substitute.
- **Where held:**
  - Pulaski County Courthouse, 100 N. Main Street, #208, Somerset, KY 42502 — marriage bonds, licenses.
  - Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA) — microfilmed county-level pre-1911 records.
  - Kentucky Department of Public Health, Office of Vital Statistics — statewide records from 1911 forward.
- **Digitized:** FamilySearch has Pulaski County marriage bonds and consent forms 1799–1871 digitized. FamilySearch also holds Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index only) and Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index only) at the statewide level.
- **Gaps:** Record-destroying disasters in 1838 and 1871 may have affected some county vital and court records. The 1871 disaster falls within the target window; verify which specific marriage, deed, and court volumes survived.
- **Access restrictions:** Birth records restricted 100 years; death records restricted 50 years; marriage records are public.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest groups in Kentucky before 1900. Local Baptist and Methodist congregations were common in rural south-central Kentucky. Source: [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials, confirmations, membership lists, and minutes.
- **Why critical:** Church registers predate and substantially fill the gaps in civil registration for 1840–1880 in Pulaski County. For the years 1840–1852 and 1863–1873, church records are the primary source for baptisms and burials.
- **Where held:**
  - FamilySearch Library microfilm — many Kentucky congregation records.
  - Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort — manuscript church records.
  - Filson Historical Society, Louisville — Baptist, Methodist, and Presbyterian records (primarily Louisville area; may hold some south-central Kentucky collections).
  - Pulaski County Historical Society — holds the most comprehensive collection of local church records, per the Pulaski County wiki page.
  - Individual denominational archives: Southern Baptist Historical Library (Nashville), various Methodist conference archives, Presbyterian Historical Society (Philadelphia).
  - Active local congregations may still hold their own records.
- **FamilySearch online collections:**
  - Kentucky Church Records, 1818–1995 — index and images (incomplete)
  - Kentucky Births and Christenings, 1839–1960 — index only
  - Kentucky Marriages, 1785–1979 — index only
  - Kentucky Deaths and Burials, 1843–1970 — index only
- **Language:** English.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Available for Pulaski County in 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880. All are indexed and have images available on both FamilySearch and Ancestry. The 1880 census also includes a Soundex index.
- **Mortality schedules:** The 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 federal mortality schedules record individuals who died in the year preceding the census — a valuable source for the death gaps in civil registration. Available on FamilySearch and Ancestry.
- **State census:** Kentucky did not conduct a state census during the 1840–1880 period. No intercensal state enumeration exists.
- **Access:** Federal census records for this period are indexed and fully accessible online at FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription).

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate inventories, administrations, guardianships, letters testamentary, court order books, equity cases.
- **Date range:** Probate records begin 1801; court records begin 1799. Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Testate or intestate:** Search will books (wills) for testate estates; administration/inventory records for intestate estates.
- **Digitized:** FamilySearch has digitized Pulaski County early will books (1801–1929). Whether these are indexed or browse-only images was not returned by volume_search in this session — treat as browse-only until confirmed.
- **Where held:**
  - Pulaski County Courthouse, Somerset — original wills, court orders, deeds.
  - KDLA — microfilmed copies of many county records.
- **Record loss note:** The 1871 disaster may have affected probate volumes filed around that date — check which volumes survived.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state with Virginia-origin surveys).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Kentucky is a state-land state. The **Kentucky Land Office**, Frankfort, holds land grants, original warrants, surveys, and patents. Do NOT use the BLM General Land Office website — it covers federal-land states and Kentucky is not among them. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Types:** Deeds (person-to-person transactions at county courthouse from 1799), land grants/patents (Kentucky Land Office), surveys, tax lists, Old Kentucky Grants (1793–1856), Kentucky Land Warrants (1816–1873).
- **Date range:** Land records begin 1799 at the county level.
- **Where held:**
  - Pulaski County Courthouse — deed books from 1799.
  - Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort — grants, warrants, surveys, patents.
  - Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort — additional land manuscripts.
- **Online:** FamilySearch has Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants and related records (1700–1955) as digitized images. Ancestry also holds Kentucky land grant records.
- **Genealogical value:** Deeds often name the wife (releasing dower rights), previous residence, and heirs — valuable when vital records are absent.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts for 1840–1880:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848), Civil War (1861–1865).
- **Civil War note:** Kentucky was a border state. Pulaski County residents served in both Union and Confederate forces. Search both Union and Confederate series at NARA.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants (Mexican-American War and Civil War), draft registrations, unit muster rolls.
- **Where held:**
  - NARA (National Archives and Records Administration) — federal military service records and pension files; Confederate service records are also at NARA.
  - Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) — military records online, subscription.
  - Kentucky State Archives, KDLA — state adjutant general records, Kentucky unit rosters.

### Cemetery records
- **Coverage:** Pulaski County has numerous family cemeteries, church cemeteries, and a few municipal burial grounds. The Pulaski County Historical Society holds local cemetery transcription surveys.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) — free; indexes many Pulaski County burials with transcribed inscriptions. BillionGraves provides additional coverage.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records (where they exist) are held by individual churches or municipal offices.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Somerset had local newspapers by the mid-19th century; the Pulaski County Historical Society holds clippings and obituary files from local papers.
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Historical Society — obituary and news clipping files organized by surname. Kentucky newspapers may be accessible through Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/, subscription) and the Kentucky Digital Newspaper Program.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate sale announcements, legal notices (land sales, court proceedings).

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Context:** Pulaski County is inland and far from major ports. Most 1840–1880 residents were multi-generation Kentuckians of colonial-era Virginia/Carolina stock; immigrant arrivals in this county during the period were relatively small.
- **Relevant ports for any immigrant arrivals:** New Orleans (common for midwestern river routes), Baltimore, New York.
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests (NARA, indexed on Ancestry and FamilySearch), naturalization records (held at county courts pre-1906), border crossing records.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.
- **Naturalization:** Pre-1906 naturalization declarations could be filed in any court of record, including the Pulaski County Circuit Court.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Kentucky county tax lists (property and personal property) assessed annually.
- **Date range:** From county formation; tax lists exist through the full 1840–1880 window.
- **Where held:** County courthouse; KDLA holds microfilmed copies. Ancestry has Kentucky county tax lists.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are invaluable substitutes for missing census years and for tracing men between censuses. A young man appearing on his own tax list for the first time can establish approximate adulthood dates. Absence from tax lists can indicate death, migration, or poverty.

### Other record types
- **Court order books:** Pulaski County Circuit Court order books from 1799 record road overseer appointments, guardian bonds, jury pools, and ordinary licenses — all naming county residents not found in other series.
- **Local and county histories:** Published county histories from the late 19th and early 20th centuries often transcribe early records and carry biographical sketches of founding families. The Pulaski County Historical Society is the best source for these.
- **School records:** Common school enrollment records may exist at the KDLA; coverage for 1840–1880 is uneven.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |

| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Will books 1801–1929; marriage bonds 1799–1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995 (partial); Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960 (index); Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index); Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index); Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955; Federal census 1840–1880 (indexed + images) | Free |

| Pulaski County Historical Society, Somerset | Surname vertical files; church records; obituary/newspaper clipping files; cemetery surveys | In-person; contact for hours |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records | In-person; some microfilm available through interlibrary loan |
